#3533. Joe Biden Has a Lot of Unknown Unknowns

Read Party Animals: A letter from the back rooms, barstools, and bacchanals of Washington, DC—with exclusive reporting, interviews, and analysis.

Good afternoon from Washington, where Party Animals has not forgotten the 5 a.m. wake-up required last Tuesday to attend Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s first Pentagon press conference in six months. This was a peculiar one, arranged so Hegseth could brief the public on his own personal battle for career survival.

The briefing kicked off at 8 a.m., but the press had to be at the Pentagon by 6 a.m. for an extensive security screening. I’d like to think that this cruel early start was a consequence of Hegseth’s self-proclaimed sobriety. What kind of drunk drags his sorry carcass before a crowd of jackals before noon? Not any I know.

But sources I spoke with for a new piece on Hegseth’s war inside the Pentagon told me there was a more Machiavellian motivation for the presser: Donald Trump loves to watch Fox & Friends at 8 a.m. And sure enough, soon after the conclusion of Hegseth’s performance, its intended audience of one offered a review on Truth Social.

Read on for my investigation into Hegseth’s turbulent tenure at the top of the Department of Defense, and what it means for his survival as Democrats take control of Congress in January.

The Atlantic calls the book “unrepentant.” The New York Times calls it a 400-page “cover letter.” The former president offers the fantastical opinion that he should have stayed in the race in 2024 and faced Trump, quite a position to maintain given he couldn’t voice his own audiobook and limited his press appearances for the release to a soft-focus People magazine story (his publisher did not respond to Party Animals’ multiple requests for an interview). According to the reviews, the former president dedicates scant attention to one of the biggest debacles of his presidency, the war in Gaza, which he abetted thanks to near-unwavering support for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu as 2,000-pound bombs rained down on the densely packed enclave, killing more than 70,000 people. As president, Biden publicly questioned the death toll numbers. “Too many innocent Palestinians were killed,” he now writes, as if possessed by the passive-voice ghost of Donald Rumsfeld. Mistakes were made, indeed. In contrast with his remarkably clinical view of dead Gazans, he writes movingly about his friendship with Netanyahu, recalling his farewell to the prime minister days before leaving the White House: “I still love you, pal.”

That this was barely noticed is a sign of just how extreme Musk’s rhetoric has become over the years, as he devolved Xeet by Xeet into the online equivalent of a bum who yells at strangers on the street about race science. Then the midterms happened. After blowing nearly $500 million in an effort to get Republicans elected and falling short in key races, particularly in Texas, the octocentibillionaire seems to be seeking some kind of public rehabilitation. In a virtual appearance at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk told Andrew Ross Sorkin that he is “not MAGA”—despite the many photos of Elon wearing a certain conspicuous hat—and that he is actually “a moderate.” Don’t take the hat’s word for it, though, here’s Musk on the record in October 2024: “I’m not just MAGA, I’m Dark MAGA.” Ah, well, nevertheless. He expressed hope for incoming Texas governor Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, and said he felt “foolish” for blowing so many millions to achieve very little. What’s the over/under on how long Moderate Elon will last?

Miller and Marco: The Wall Street Journal has a great report on the close relationship between Stephen Miller and Marco Rubio, who have forged an unlikely alliance despite their past clashes over policy like immigration. It’s a revealing look at how Rubio’s Republican Party lost to Miller’s Republican Party, and how Rubio then jettisoned his entire worldview to join the winning team.

Trump of Wall Street: The Washington Post reports that Trump’s financial disclosure revealed he held between $13 million and $62 million in Nvidia stock as of the end of August. That’s considerably higher than the $615,000 to $1.3 million he held at the end of 2024.

French, Toast: No one should know who “Bo” French is. No one really did until the Republican candidate for Texas Railroad Commission went viral for complaining about a group of college kids celebrating a touchdown at a University of Texas football game. (Some of the kids were not white; French objected to this). He became whatever the opposite of a sensation is and ended up losing his election to a Democrat. Now Politico reports French has taken another blow: River Crest Country Club, the Fort Worth members institution he frequented, has kicked him out.

Garcia’s Hit List: Robert Garcia, the House Democrat who is expected to lead the Oversight Committee in the new Congress, has begun mapping out his targets. Per The Atlantic: “Garcia this morning sent a dozen letters to high-ranking Trump-administration officials and members of the president’s family, providing the clearest signal yet of which topics—and which people—will likely face the greatest scrutiny once Democrats take control of the House.”

Oversight O’clock: New York Magazine’s Ben Terris went deep on the new era of Democratic oversight, everything from the war with Iran to Trump’s big beautiful ballroom.

No Longer Satire: Read Joe Bernstein, writing for The New York Times Magazine, on how America is becoming more and more like Grand Theft Auto.

Bye-Bye Boebert: Annie Karni writes for The New York Times about the rise and fall of the MAGA Mean Girl Caucus, as Marjorie Taylor Greene, Lauren Boebert, and Nancy Mace all exit Congress.

All the endings (and a couple variations) for GTA 6 we've seen so far.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Obviously, massive spoilers follow for GTA 6 endings!

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and while we haven't experienced them all personally here at PC Gamer, the gaming community has been sharing them around for anyone curious about what they may have missed.

The ending you get depends on the choices you make during the final GTA 6 story mission, but also depends on how you handled Jason and Lucia's romance and criminal profiles throughout the game, so seeing every version of the ending would mean not just playing the ending multiple times, but having different playthroughs of the game altogether.

There are a couple of endings that I don't consider "different" from each other but do have some differences leading up to them, which I'll explain below. There may also be additional endings we haven't seen yet, so we may update this guide in the future.

In the bridge endings, Jason and Lucia have defeated Mendez and his squad and gotten the hard drive back from Georgio's penthouse and escaped. They drive to Cal's place in Key Lento, but discover he has been compromised. They drive to the bridge, but the cops have set up a roadblock and have the couple trapped. Lucia wants to keep going, but Jason suggests they jump off the bridge and swim for it.

A choice comes up on the screen: "Swim For it" or "No Surrender."

Jason and Lucia try to run the roadblock and are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, we see that their son Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, their lawyer, Abe, brings the money to Lucia's aunt. Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children in a much bigger house than the other No Surrender ending.

Choosing "Swim for it" presents an additional choice. When Jason gets out of the car, Lucia can choose to "Exit" the car with him, or change her mind by not choosing it.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. They both exit the car without holding guns. Lucia jumps, but Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Lucia signs a deal for immunity while Jason goes to prison. Lucia gets a job in a diner. Lucia takes Tomas to meet Jason in prison, but he can only see his son through a glass divider.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. Jason exits the car with a gun, but Lucia changes her mind and stays in the car. The police open fire and Jason and Lucia are both shot to death. Tomas lives with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it, Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Two years later, Lucia uses the savings account to get Jason freed from prison. Lucia goes to the prison to pick up Jason. Jason meets Tomas and holds his hand.

If you don't have a strong relationship between Jason and Lucia, there is a different ending location: the base of Georgio's tower. In these endings, the couple never makes it to the bridge. You can also choose to break up the couple, either as Jason or as Lucia, as you begin the mission Protective Custody.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront the couple at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia has a choice to "Stay down" or "Defend Jason". She stays down and watches Jason die. Lucia is arrested, signs a deal, and visits Tomas at her aunt's house. Lucia then leaves Tomas with her aunt, takes out a gun, and continues her life of crime by preparing to rob a diner.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront them at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia chooses "Defend Jason" and fights the cops. They die together.

On the way down to ground level at the tower, Jason decides to run. Lucia is arrested and signs the deal, then lives with her aunt and Tomas while working in a diner. One night there's a knock on the door and she finds a bag of cash on the porch. We see Jason driving away with... Rocco the drug-sniffing dog from earlier in the game. Sure, that might as well happen.

How to get this ending (sourced by GamingwithTZ on YouTube):

Jason and Lucia make a deal with Mendez after defeating him. Once they have the hard drive, they're surrounded by cops at the bottom of the tower. Mendez arrives and takes them away in his car, then drives them to the swamp. Later in the credits, we see two skulls in the swamp, side-by-side, with a bullet hole in each.

Note: You may need a specific criminal profile for this ending. I tried to take the deal (as Lucia) in one of my ending playthroughs, but Jason shot Mendez anyway. I had both Jason and Lucia at "Professional" level criminal profiles. This ending was not available to me. Speculation, but this ending may only be available if you don't have "Professional" as your criminal profiles.

There are potentially (and almost certainly) more endings to GTA 6. There are still a few combinations of all the different variables, including your romance level, criminal profile level, amount of money saved, and the choices you make during the final mission, that we haven't seen yet.

We'll update this guide if the community finds more endings.

#3531. GTA 6’s Console Wars Are Already Over, And Xbox Lost

Grand Theft Auto games have never shied away from satirizing life, and GTA 6 has plenty of digs at famous brands, trends, and people. Not even gaming is immune to GTA's patented satire, especially if you're playing on Xbox, because there's no escape from PlayStation — or its legally distinct cousin, the JoySystem.

Early in GTA 6, you'll get to bond with Jason's best pal, Cal. After maximizing the energy of Jason's bachelor pad with a little feng shui redecorating, the duo settles in for a night of booze, drugs, and video games on Booby's JoyStation console, which looks very similar to a PS5. It looks like this is the only gaming hardware in Leonida, since there are no Xbox Egg-Cube Stations X to play games on.

The JoySystem isn't just for decoration either; after you've hung out with Bobby, you can return and play games on it. You can choose between an avant-garde experience or more immediate gratification with a pair of shooter games, and it's impressive how good these three games are on their own. From top-down action to stunning mystery that pokes fun at auteur-driven games, they're worth checking out. The JoySystem interface is also a 1:1 copy of the PS5 user interface, with the exact same layout for games and other apps — but given how much Sony is making from GTA 6 sales, we're guessing the company sees it as a cheeky little homage.

But the controllers for the console? They look terrible:

In real life, PS5 sales have absolutely dominated GTA 6 preorders and sales. Video game research company Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 sales have reached 24.58 million total units via pre-purchases and copies sold at launch, which works out to about $2.36 billion in gross revenue. Of that number, 18.44 million units are said to be PS5 copies of the game, of which Sony will get a 30% cut of sales.

For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

#3530. Hacker Threatens To Leak Free Version Of GTA 6 In Crypto Grift

Somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned. This time, the infamous leaker is threatening to release the executable file for a working build of the Xbox version of the game hosted on their site, provided the public helps raise their meme coin to a $15 million market cap.

"It is done. CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent," a statement from Cyberleek reads (via Kotaku). "Now. Every file except one--the main executable--held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons."

The files on Cyberleek's site reportedly clock in at over 200GB, which would line up with the Xbox version of the game, but there's no guarantee they're the actual GTA 6 data or a collection of malware waiting to be downloaded onto a PC. The hacker added that if their demands aren't met, they'll release the executable needed to play GTA 6. However, there's no guarantee the game can be emulated, and Cyberleek added that they'll "work to get a PS5 build" if people keep supporting them.

This isn't the first time Cyberleek has threatened to release a pirated build of GTA 6; back in October, they promised to do so if their meme coin reached $30 million in value. While this didn't happen--and the coin eventually crashed out--they did drop several GTA 6 video clips throughout the month showing off more of the game in action. While Cyberleek initially claimed to act in gamers' interests when they first burst onto the scene, they true motives were quickly revealed when they started hyping up their meme coin--reportedly part of a pump-and-dump scheme.

While Cyberleek has yet to be identified, their actions did lead to GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games to issue a statement, in which it described the leaks as "heartbreaking" after years of work on the game. Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two, filed multiple subpoenas, asking Microsoft and Discord to help identify CyberLeek. So far, the hacker remains a mystery.

I can’t believe the release of Sunrise on the Reaping means I’ve been going to the theaters for The Hunger Games movies for nearly fifteen years! I’ll never forget when I went to see one of my favorite novels at the time become a book-to-screen adaptation back in 2012. I just rewatched the franchise and recalled one gripe I had about the movie when I first saw it that I actually understand now as an adult.

These days I think the original The Hunger Games movie is pretty great, and I’ve rewatched it so many times. I remember when I went to see it back then, I thought it was a faithful adaptation, but I was bummed that they decided to take out the fact that Peeta loses his leg in The Hunger Games. Check out this excerpt from the end of the first book:

Caesar asks Peeta how his 'new leg' is working out. 'New leg?' I say, and I can't help reaching out and pulling up the bottom of Peeta's pants. 'Oh, no,' I whisper,' taking in the metal-and-plastic device that has replaced his flesh.

In the movie, Peeta gets injured like in the book, but Katniss nurses him back to health, and he completely recovers by the end. Yet, in the source material, Peeta is practically bleeding out right before they become the final people in the arena. Katniss is desperate to help him, and she suggests they both have poisonous berries so she can save them both. When they reunite for the post-victory interview with Caesar Flickerman, she learns that his leg had to be amputated right after they left the arena.

I think when The Hunger Games movie came out, I thought the movie was censoring an important aspect of the story. Peeta’s major injury really had me on the edge of my seat while I was reading the book, so it was sort of anticlimactic for the movie to completely skip it.

However, it just dawned on me during my recent rewatch (with my Hulu subscription) that I haven’t thought about this change to The Hunger Games in a really long time. I guess, ultimately, it didn’t really matter that Peeta only has one leg in the scope of the whole series, and it probably would have caused some extra special effects headaches for the filmmaking team.

There’s something else. Ultimately, I’m realizing that both Peeta and Katniss have so many horrific things happen to them throughout the series that maybe it was OK for the movies to skip Peeta losing a leg. I mean, what happens to Peeta in Mockingjay alone is just heartbreaking. The guy loses his entire family, he’s captured by the Capitol and starved. And then, his brain is altered so he thinks Katniss is his enemy. That’s some really rough stuff.

Now, I think overall The Hunger Games movie series did a great job of adapting the maturity of the book series, but now I’m OK with the films taking out a few extra traumatic things like Peeta’s amputated leg.

#3528. Brielle Biermann Wants to Break Out From Behind Mom Kim Zolciak’s Shadow

Brielle Biermann got candid about the pros and cons of growing up in the public eye with her Bravo star mom, Kim Zolciak.

“I definitely want to be my own person. I think that was kind of the theme here today with everybody,” she exclusively told Us on set of Celebrity Weakest Link’s “Next Generation” episode, which also included Joseph Baena, Sailor Brinkley-Cook, Cori Broadus, Corinne Foxx, Prince Jackson, Hailie Jade Scott and Melissa Rivers. “I am Brielle Biermann first and Kim’s daughter second.”

Biermann, who recently tied the knot with Billy Seidl in Florida, is determined to pave her own way.

“I want people to remember that and know that I have my own identity,” she noted. “So I’m trying to be more conscientious about those types of shows or opportunities and decisions going forward so that way I can really branch out and be my own person.”

Before competing for her charity of choice — World Central Kitchen — on the Fox game show, Biermann and her family were featured on The Real Housewives of Atlanta from 2008 to 2012. Zolciak, 48, subsequently received her own spinoff show titled Don’t Be Tardy for the Wedding, which focused on her nuptials with Kroy Biermann. The series was later renamed to Don’t Be Tardy and continued to air until 2020.

Having her life featured on reality TV taught Brielle some important lessons.

“I think resilience and being a survivor. You can go through and grow through anything. So nothing ever knocks me down,” she told Us. “I’ve been to hell and back many times — as people can read. And here I am.”

Celebrity Weakest Link allowed Brielle to show a new side of herself — but it was still a challenge.

“Oh, I am 100 percent competitive. But I also have a lot of empathy,” she noted. “So it’s hard because I feel really bad sending somebody home.”

The experience also made Brielle want to do more reality shows.

“Special Forces is a little scary, but sure I’ll do it,” she said. “Gia [Giudice]’s experience is a little crazy. I saw a couple of her episodes. I’m down for anything, honestly. This year is all about embracing awkwardness and saying yes. I want to do something scary every single day. So here is my scary [thing] and it was actually really amazing.”

Celebrity Weakest Link airs on Fox Mondays at 9 p.m. ET.

#3527. GTA 6 Is A British Success Story, Prime Minister Says, But He Won’t Play It

The Prime Minister of the UK, Andy Burnham, has labeled Rockstar Games a "British success story" amid GTA 6's rave reviews and huge sales milestones.

A spokesperson for his office told The Independent, "Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh, and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait."

Rockstar North is based in Edinburgh, Scotland, but GTA 6 was made by thousands of people across the globe. GTA is also historically linked to the UK, as the original game, 1997's Grand Theft Auto, was made by DMA Design in Edinburgh.

Asked if the PM himself would play GTA 6, his office said Burnham is too busy right now. "He won't be playing it," the spokesperson said.

GTA 6 launched on November 19 and reportedly sold nearly 25 million copies and earned $2 billion in revenue by launch day. The game boasts a mightily impressive 99 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic, meaning it's tied with the original Ocarina of Times for the highest aggregate review score for any game ever.

GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, but many are expecting Rockstar to eventually announce an online mode for the game. According to reports, the new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could arrive in 2027, with a PC edition also coming that year.

#3526. Kristen Bell, Andie MacDowell, Eva Longoria, and More Honor Community Builders at L’Oréal Paris’s Women of Worth Gala

L’Oréal Paris welcomed its latest Women of Worth honorees with an intimate, elegant gala in Los Angeles on Wednesday night. For the annual celebration, which honors unsung nonprofit leaders, guests gathered at The Ebell of Los Angeles, a venue with a rich history of its own.

The evening began with an outdoor cocktail hour, where guests enjoyed passed apps and specialty drinks like the “Parisian Refresher” and “Worth It Spritz” under sparkling bistro lights. As honorees and attendees mixed and mingled, they also had the opportunity to pose for a photographer and peruse a beauty bar stocked with L’Oréal Paris-brand lipsticks, lip oils, and glosses, which were available for guests to take home in a plush velvet bag with “I’m Worth It” embroidered on it.

As the gala officially began inside The Ebell’s picturesque ballroom, longtime brand ambassador Eva Longoria gave the introductory remarks, noting that “this night always gives me goosebumps. I’m always crying.” She saluted her 20-plus-year partnership with the brand and joked that it made her “112 years old,” though she doesn’t look like it, the actor-director said, “because I use Revitalift.” She gave a shout-out to the many beauty influencers in attendance, including Laura Lee and Desi Perkins. “You guys really changed the game of beauty, and I just applaud you,” she said. “Put me in your TikToks.”

L’Oréal Paris USA president Laura Branik followed Longoria, emphasizing the brand’s commitment to and pride in its Women of Worth program, which continues to celebrate “the power of women who know their worth and use it,” she said. She then welcomed the company’s newest global ambassador, Kristen Bell, to the stage. Bell, who was attending her “first Women of Worth ever,” said she was “very happy to be here” and introduced moving presentations for the first two honorees: Vy Le of WhereWear, which transforms clothing donations into targeted support for women’s and housing-insecure shelters and the people they serve, and Amanda Rice of The Chick Mission, a nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that every young woman newly diagnosed with cancer has the option to preserve her fertility.

Actor and brand ambassador Aja Naomi King was up next, taking note of the room full of glamorous gowns and festive energy. “Everyone showed up and showed out,” she said, “and we appreciate that because these women deserve to be celebrated properly. I had the immense honor of helping select this year’s Women of Worth, and I keep thinking about how much it matters when someone believes in your potential.” King introduced two honorees: Maya Bird-Murphy of Mobile Makers, an award-winning nonprofit that expands access to design education through workshops, community engagement, public installations, and pop-ups, and Christy Vogel of Sounding Joy, a nonprofit dedicated to providing hearing aids to children whose families cannot afford them.

Longoria then returned to present another pair of honorees: Marisa Hamamoto of Infinite Flow Dance, an award-winning disability-led nonprofit and professional dance company with a mission to reimagine possibilities, one dance at a time, and Chanel Power of Mentor Me Collective, a technical institute transforming how emerging technologists are identified, developed, and positioned to lead.

During a break in the program, guests enjoyed dinner from a menu that included roast chicken, citrus-soy-and-apple-cider-braised short ribs, and vegan pan-seared “scallops.” Another highlight? The venue’s bathrooms were stocked with more coveted L’Oréal Paris goods like lip oil, mascara, setting spray, and velour puff makeup applicators.

Following the break, ambassador, actor, and model Cara Delevingne led the room in a cheerful group proclamation of “We’re worth it!” before introducing her honorees: Emily Cho of Juvie for STEM (JSTEM), an international nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to high-quality STEM education for justice-involved youth, and Arielle Galinsky of The Legacy Project, Inc. (TLP), a national nonprofit connecting younger and older adults for multigenerational friendship and storytelling.

Legacy L’Oréal Paris ambassador Andie MacDowell had the pleasure of introducing the event’s final honorees. “For 40 years I have been a part of the L’Oréal Paris family,” she said, with the milestone receiving enthusiastic applause from the audience. “After all these years, the thing that stays with me [about the Women of Worth honorees] is the determination to make life better for someone else. That kind of care is powerful.” MacDowell introduced Jordan Pine of Greenlight Operation, a Pennsylvania nonprofit that strives to strategically combat human trafficking and serve sex trafficked women through a continuum of restorative care, and Dr. Christie Brungardt, cofounder of Jana’s Campaign, a Kansas-based nonprofit dedicated to preventing gender and relationship violence through education.

Proud “newbie” Bell returned to the stage to offer closing remarks and thank all the honorees for their tireless efforts to make life better for others. “I will be thinking of all 10 of these stories and the women we met tonight for quite some time,” she said. “Even though their stories couldn’t be more different, they seem to have one thing in common: that they all saw what needed to change and they did it. They didn’t wait for someone else to do something; they stepped forward and they did it themselves. And honestly, I think that’s gonna be my biggest takeaway from my first Women of Worth celebration ever: Never underestimate what one woman can set in motion.”

Each of the 10 Women of Worth 2026 honorees received a $25,000 grant, mentorship, and national visibility. As the program concluded, honorees, their proud guests, and other attendees continued to soak up the special evening and shared in a few more hugs and photo ops. Before departing for the evening, guests were invited to enjoy a final “sweet moment” in a separate room where a colorful candy bar and glasses of Champagne awaited.

Woll will portray Faye, the "mysterious" wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Deborah Ann Woll said she felt "totally unbothered" by the small but vocal subset of gamers who were upset by the upcoming God of War: Laufey, and apparently she meant it—because today Amazon MGM Studios announced that she's going to play the same role in the live-action God of War series coming to Prime.

Just as in God of War: Laufey and its predecessor, God of War: Ragnarok, Woll—best known for playing Karen Page in Marvel's Daredevil, Defenders, and Punisher TV series, as well as a lengthy stint on True Blood as Jessica Hamby—will portray Faye, wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus.

"Faye’s abrupt passing sets in motion the events of God of War," the announcement says. "Along their journey, Kratos and Atreus discover secrets about Faye that make them wonder how well they truly knew her at all."

It's been a bumpy road for the God of War series. It was first reported in 2022, but started over from scratch two years later after the showrunner and executive producers quit. We got our first look at Ryan Hurst as Kratos earlier this year—not very impressive, but we all had the same initial impression of Henry Cavill as Geralt and that worked out well—but then Hurst had to be recast because of an on-set injury; Dave Bautista now has the lead role. Child actors Callum Vinson and Island Austin, who played Atreus and Thrud, were also recast.

God of War: Laufey is set to launch on May 20, 2027, but sadly is a PlayStation 5 exclusive, a state of affairs that seems likely to endure given Sony's recent strategy shift. The God of War live action series on Prime has been ordered for two seasons, but a release target hasn't been announced.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

#3524. These Pokemon Anniversary Fender Guitars Have A Secret Weapon: Game Boy Sounds

The Pokemon franchise turned 30 this year, and while you'll have to wait until next year for a new mainline game installment, you can celebrate that anniversary with something that's much cooler: Rock-and-roll-type electric guitars.

The Pokemon Company revealed that it teamed up with guitar manufacturer Fender to produce a Stratocaster model inspired by Pokemon Red, and a Telecaster model inspired by Pokemon Green. Each guitar features an aesthetic that pays tribute to the original Pokemon Game Boy adventures, including pixel art pulled from the games, graphics, and color overlays for an extra pop.

The guitars really shine with a special toggle that warps the music they produce into an 8-bit retro sound that’s reminiscent of vintage gaming hardware. The neck also pays homage to Pokemon, with a special design that commemorates the collaboration between Fender and Pokemon. Just remember: No Stairway.

As you'd expect, these won't be cheap. While US pricing and availability will be confirmed later on the Pokemon Center retail site, in Japan, these will retail for around $2,600 each. You'll also need to enter a lottery to stand a chance at winning the option to purchase one of these Fenders, which should prevent the items from being pounced on en masse by Pokemon scalpers.

This year has seen several promotions kick off to celebrate 30 years of Pokemon, and one of the biggest involved Krispy Kreme. The doughnut chain's boxes of digestible pocket monsters proved highly popular, and unsurprisingly, Pokemon scalpers wasted no time trying to flip those treats and packaging for cash online. At least the legally distinct Pokemoan sex toys re-released this year proved to be somewhat immune to scalper efforts.

Holiday time at Walt Disney World is always one of the best times to visit, but theme park fans might want to postpone their trips to the “Most Magical Place on Earth” until later in 2027. That's when all the new and upcoming attractions are slated to open, like the new Indiana Jones ride in Animal Kingdom. In case anyone has been wondering, Imagineers have been hard at work on the ride, and they’re finally giving fans a first look at the magic they’re crafting.

The new Indiana Jones attraction was announced back in September 2025 at Disney’s Destination D23 event in Orlando, Florida. The news was originally met with concern from Disney World enthusiasts. It’s always exciting to see a park get a new ride, especially Animal Kingdom, which currently has the fewest amount of rides out of the four parks. However, the introduction of Indiana Jones meant the loss of the beloved Animal Kingdom attraction Dinosaur.

Time heals most wounds, though, and now that the sting of losing Dinosaur has started to wane, most fans are finally getting excited for the new attraction. To further build excitement, Walt Disney Imagineering shared the following clip on its Instagram:

A post shared by Walt Disney Imagineering & Disney Live Entertainment (@waltdisneyimagineering)

I was definitely not thrilled about the Animal Kingdom changes at first, but I think I’m going to love this new version of Indiana Jones! I’m definitely on board with the name that was announced back at D23 earlier this year, and I absolutely love the Mayan-inspired facade. Dare I say it puts the Indiana Jones temple at Disneyland to shame (and hopefully won't have to deal with brawls over line cutting).

I Honestly Never Thought I’d Live To See The Day Disney World Fixed One Broken Attraction

When the ride eventually opens sometime next year, guests will embark on an adventure alongside Indy that will take them to a temple that legend says has a water passageway that leads to an underworld protected by a mythic serpent. Imagineers are still keeping much of the actual ride experience under wraps for now. However, with two other cart-style Indiana Jones attractions at other Disney parks and reports that the Dinosaur ride is being rethemed instead of totally demolished, it’s safe to say that this version of Indiana Jones will take guests on a bumpy ride full of twists, turns, snakes (or serpents in this case), and adventure.

Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent will be found in the new Tropical Americas expansion at Disney’s Animal Kingdom. Specifically, the thrill ride will be part of the Bonanche Bioreseve area of the expansion, which is being modeled after the Maya region. This will mark the second Indy attraction to explore Mayan culture, but the first in the United States.

Perhaps the most exciting thing about the new ride is that real-life Indiana Jones actor Harrison Ford was used as the model for the attraction’s animatronic. While it’s not confirmed whether or not he’ll record lines too, I’m definitely hoping he will. And if he does, then this will definitely be the best Indy ride.

There’s still a lot of work to be done on the Indiana Jones ride and the Tropical Americas land, which will include a section dedicated to Encanto. For now, fans can keep the excitement going by streaming the adventure franchise with an active Disney+ subscription.

#3521. GTA 7? Please, Let GTA 6 Cook First, Take-Two CEO Says

Rockstar Games just launched Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19 to rave reviews and huge sales. Everyone wants to know what's coming next, and surely there will eventually be another GTA game, but not soon.

Appearing on OpenAI's technology and business show TBPN recently, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked how a new GTA game could possibly up the ante. TBPN's Jordi Hays theorized that GTA 7 could "be a live version of the entire world."

Zelnick, for his part, said people should remember that the interview was recorded on November 19, the day that GTA 6 released, so it's not time to talk about GTA 7.

"I can't help myself. We at Take-Two just went live GTA 6 on November 19. Let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19. And you're asking a question about GTA 7," he said.

While Rockstar isn't talking about GTA 7 yet--and no one should expect that to happen anytime soon--Take-Two has already signaled that the next GTA game could come out sooner.

He said the “nature and velocity” of the company’s content releases in its major franchises, including GTA, will look “dramatically different over the next decade.”

GTA 6 released more than 13 years after GTA 5 came out in 2013. However, development didn't begin in earnest on GTA 6 until after Red Dead Redemption II came out in 2018, according to reporter Jason Schreier. This is because Rockstar's network of studios around the world work together on one project at a time, though smaller teams are also cooking up new things simultaneously.

For more, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first.

Spoiler: It doesn't actually run at 60 fps.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found a glitch with the Xbox version of the game that allows players to forcibly remove Rockstar's 30 fps cap. But even though people claim the game jumps up to 60 fps, the actual performance is nowhere near as smooth, according to Digital Foundry's tests.

The glitch is surprisingly simple to perform: You just need to set the console's output to 60 Hz, load GTA 6, swap the output to 120 Hz, load a different game, and then use the Quick Resume feature to go back to GTA 6. For whatever reason, this forces the game to run above 30 fps, but not by much.

In Digital Foundry's testing, GTA 6 doesn't suddenly become a buttery smooth 60 fps dream. Instead, it has an average frame rate of about 36 fps and still drops below that number during particularly intense scenes, like in city areas or when multiple cars are exploding due to rocket launcher hijinks.

The most notable improvement is lower input lag when it manages to climb up to around 40 fps, but even that has an asterisk because the frame rate varies too much for the benefits to be consistent. Unless you plan on spending your time in Leonida roleplaying as a fisherman, you're going to have a bad time.

While Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said an official 60 fps mode for GTA 6 is too much for the current generation of consoles to handle, including the PS5 Pro, Digital Foundry theorizes that a 40 fps mode might be possible in the future.

I'm hopeful for console players, but none of this has stopped me from wanting the game on the only platform where 60 fps won't be much of a challenge to hit: PC. Tweaking settings you don't care as much about to juice the frame rate is much preferable over having to deal with a set "performance" mode or a glitch that could be patched out any day. A good PC version should be able to nicely scale up or down in performance based on your hardware setup, and Rockstar has shown that it can pull that off in the past with games like Red Dead Redemption 2.

For a game as good as GTA 6—Chris says it's "(mostly) great" in his 100-hour impressions— you shouldn't have to deal with quirks that tarnish the experience. I'm not a Rockstar employee, I don't know what challenges a PC version introduces or why it wasn't prioritized for a simultaneous PC and console release, but I do know that a PC version likely won't have as many caveats when it comes to performance as it does on consoles. So, I'll deal with Rockstar's intended 30 fps cap until the moment I can boot up GTA 6 on my PC, and then forget that I ever had to endure the limits of the current console experience.

#3519. GTA 6 Doesn’t Have Any Doja Cat Music, And She Didn’t Censor Her Message To Rockstar

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is out now, and the game features a lot of music from famous real-world artists. But Doja Cat is not among them.

She's not happy about that, either.

Doja Cat said online that she is "so f**kin bitter" about that. In follow-up posts, she told Rockstar to "eat my d**k." She said she loves GTA 6, and being left out of the game breaks her heart. Directing her posts at Rockstar in this way, with this language, is unlikely to win her any fans at the studio, so it would be surprising indeed if we see her music get added to the game at any point.

Doja Cat's music is not on any of GTA 6's in-game radio stations, nor do any of her tunes feature on the 34-song GTA 6: The Album, which is out now. The album includes music from Travis Scott, Dua Lipa, Morgan Wallen, Young Thug, Cardi B, Keith Richards, Lana Del Rey, and more.

The in-game radio stations, meanwhile, feature music from Tom Petty, George Strait, Glen Campbell, Bad Bunny, Drake, Lil Wayne, Slayer, Sepultura, System of a Down, and Tool, just to name few.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you're eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

The actor shared a little about their conversation.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The late Patrick Stewart was best known for his work in Star Trek, as he became synonymous with the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard. With that, it's funny to think that the beloved star ever had reservations about joining the iconic sci franchise. Now, his friend and actor Kyle MacLachlan is opening up about that apprehension, and I can't believe I never knew Stewart rang him up shortly before he committed to The Next Generation.

MacLachlan caught up with SFX Magazine on CinemaBlend recently as part of a cover story publishes shortly before Stewart's death. The Twin Peaks star talked about his long-running friendship with Stewart over the decades. Said relationship began when they worked together on the original film adaptation of Dune. A few years later, Stewart would be in the position to take on the role of Picard, and he had questions for MacLachlan before committing:

He was about to embark on this huge experience and recognized that it could potentially be both a huge benefit and that it could come with certain... restrictions isn’t the right word, but I guess he was weighing it all up.

Based on those comments, it seemed Patrick Stewart had some concerns about committing to a TV series, which could potentially air for a while and prevent him from taking on other roles as an actor. He probably had a lot on his mind, as MacLachlan said, wondering if the benefit of joining Trek would outweigh the missed opportunities elsewhere.

I've written a lot in recent weeks about how Stewart rose to prominence due to being cast in The Next Generation. However, he had to put in the work to solidify his role as one of Star Trek's best characters. As Kyle MacLachlan added, though, Stewart's fears were unfounded, as he crushed it in the job and went on to be known for other roles as well:

I thought he would be spectacular in it. He’s such a strong actor, and he’s done so many different things that he would be able to fit it into his wonderful career. It wouldn’t be the only thing that he was known for, but part of a much larger tapestry.

That tapestry of work will extend to the end of the 2026 movie schedule, as the late Stewart will appear as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday later this year. Stewart reportedly told co-stars backstage that it would be his final acting performance, marking his retirement. Stewart would refute those claims months later, saying that he considered acting to be something he would do his entire life.

Knowing that, and seeing that he truly was passionate about his acting career, gives me an immense amount of respect for Patrick Stewart. He worked because he loved the job, but I'd like to think he had a good deal of respect for his fans as well. Surely, between Marvel and Trek, he could've retired more than a decade ago, but he kept at it!

The late A Christmas Carol star's commitment to his craft is a big reason why so many fellow stars have been paying tribute to him since his passing. It's clear he was a beloved figure in Hollywood, and the world is just a little darker now that he's gone.

I'm thankful for Kyle MacLachlan being bullish on Patrick Stewart joining Star Trek: The Next Generation. Had he not been, who knows if Stewart would've taken the job. Fortunately, the Fallout actor felt good about his former co-star taking on the role, and the rest is history.

Watch Patrick Stewart in TNG by picking up a Paramount+ subscription and revisiting some of his best episodes. There are quite a few to get through, and as someone who recently started rewatching the series, I know that from experience.

#3517. ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Director Francis Lawrence on the Film’s Final Scene

When Francis Lawrence, the filmmaker behind The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, greets me over Zoom, he’s aware that his darkly lit, gothic backdrop makes him look a bit like the villainous President Snow. “All I need is a big eagle back here,” the white-haired, smartly dressed director jokes.

Lawrence has helmed almost every film in Lionsgate’s blockbuster series, based on Suzanne Collins’s best-selling novels about a dystopia where a bloodthirsty dictator forces children to fight to the death for the elite’s entertainment. He joined the franchise for its 2013 sequel, Catching Fire, and has directed only three non–Hunger Games movies in the decade-plus since. In that time, one could argue, the world has tilted further toward the oppressive future depicted in Collins’s novels—see, for instance, Donald Trump’s Hunger Games–esque Patriot Games. And while Lawrence isn’t naming names, he’s never lost sight of the movies’ larger political message. “I feel really lucky to be able to tell stories that matter, that are wrapped in these commercial packages,” he tells Vanity Fair. “So anytime one of these things comes around, I jump at it.”

Just as the original Hunger Games film made a star of Oscar winner Jennifer Lawrence (who returns for a scene in the new movie), Sunrise on the Reaping introduces the world to Australian newcomer Joseph Zada. He plays the younger version of Woody Harrelson’s Haymitch Abernathy, a victor of the Hunger Games who later serves as a mentor to actor Lawrence’s Katniss Everdeen. Making a reflective movie prompted director Lawrence to reflect on his own Hollywood trajectory. “The biggest difference is that I’m a lot more relaxed. I was nervous as hell on Catching Fire,” he says. “It was my fourth movie. It was a movie I was inheriting. It was a big movie, and it was a massive cast. So I was really intimidated. Now I have much more fun, I will say. I’m much more comfortable with actors, and the amount of actors, and with logistics. And there’s definitely a family that’s built into it, which is very important for me. There’s, what, 14 years of my life spent making these movies? So it has to be fun.”

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: When did you become aware of Sunrise on the Reaping, and at what point did you and Suzanne Collins start discussing an adaptation?

Francis Lawrence: When we did the original series of movies, and we finished the last Mockingjay, she said she was done, and we thought that was it. Then she surprised me and Nina [Jacobson], the producer, with Ballad, however many years later. And she never tells us when she’s writing. Even when she has something to read, she never tells us what it’s about. She’s very superstitious about it all. So we got the call, which was very exciting. And she said, “Go to my agent’s house. There’s a manuscript. Let’s talk after you read it.”

I got to his house, sat in his backyard, and there was a manuscript and a copy of Catching Fire sitting on top of it with a few tabs in it. I opened to the tabs and saw that it had the portion where Katniss and Peeta were looking up the Haymitch Games, that sequence from the book. And I was like, Oh, she’s written the Haymitch story, which was very exciting. And that started the process that we always have, which is that I read the manuscript in one sitting, then read it a second time after having a conversation with Suzanne.

Then I fly to New York and meet her at Scholastic, and we sit up in a conference room for about a week going through the book, beat by beat, of what we think the movie is going to be. She and I lay it all out and chat, and she sits on her computer and writes a scriptment. Then that’s the thing that we turn over to the screenwriter.

How have you built that trust with the author of these books, having adapted them for more than a decade now?

That working process happened accidentally when I signed on to do Catching Fire. I had never done a sequel to someone else’s first movie before. And when Lionsgate and the first director, [Gary Ross], parted ways and I got the call, they didn’t have a script, but they had started the process of developing it before I was on board. And so I signed on based on the book and had planned a trip to New York to meet with Suzanne.

The script came on the day that I was traveling to New York. I read it, and it was not the movie that I wanted to make—because I loved the book, and it was not the book. Luckily, nobody else wanted to make that version of the movie either. Our meeting of me just picking her brain turned into, “This script doesn’t work. Let’s go through, page by page, and figure out the version of the movie we want to make.”

That’s what really formed the bond—just working really, really closely with her. Spending 8 or 10 hours a day for a week or two in a conference room—me riffing on visual ideas and her talking about the story. We think the same way in terms of storytelling, structure, and she seemed to take to my visual ideas.

There’s this weird dynamic that happens as we get closer to production. We’re usually developing the script pretty much within a week of shooting. But the production is also building. So you have thousands of people working, figuring out locations, traveling in different parts of the world. The stress levels are building.

Suzanne and I have related the relationship to almost like a mother-son relationship. It starts really lovely and creative, but then as we get closer and closer, it’s me being that late teen who’s ready to leave the home, like, Okay, enough’s enough. I’m going to go make the movie now. I have to say, I love the process. It’s not without its stress sometimes, but that’s part of the closeness of it all that I cherish.

How did this film’s futuristic-meets-1970s aesthetic come about?

There was an element [of the story] that reminded me a bit of Alice in Wonderland, which then made me think of Jefferson Airplane, that song “White Rabbit,” which brought me to the ’60s and ’70s. Then you can look at characters certain ways. Like, Haymitch, you go, Okay, he’s from, like, young Bruce Springsteen, or Lenore Dove [played by Whitney Peak], like a young Stevie Nicks. And you get this hippie vibe. And the Capitol is that Warhol Studio 54 crowd, and Snow like a ’70s Yves Saint Laurent.

How do you go about casting a young Haymitch, finding an actor who can anchor the film like Jennifer Lawrence did in the original Hunger Games film?

Our casting director, Deb Zane, had met him, and I want to say before he did East of Eden. She had a lot of faith in him. We liked his self-tape a lot. But we knew that he was going to have to pull a lot off. He starts as a very optimistic, fun, playful, young guy in love, and in this movie has to turn into somebody that’s much closer to the Haymitch that we’re used to—cynical and a drunk. He’s going to have to go through a lot of emotional trauma, plus have that kind of mischievousness, irreverence, all these different elements that Woody [Harrelson] has naturally. And so we really put him through the ringer. We did a lot of tests, kept bringing him back, bringing him back, bringing him back. He and I were modulating how much Woody we feel in his performance.

I want to make sure that everybody makes the role their own. That they find the spirit of the character and that it’s not trying to do an imitation of somebody. That’s true of Elle [Fanning] doing Effie, of Ralph [Fiennes] doing Snow, of Jesse [Plemons] doing Plutarch, Kieran [Culkin] as Caesar. Everybody has to figure out how to do it on their own. Then the weird thing is that Kelvin [Harrison Jr., who plays a young Beetee], has worked with Jeffrey [Wright] three times. So he’s fairly close with Jeffrey. When he got the role, he called and said, “You won’t believe this, but I’m actually playing the young version of you.” He could just conjure Jeffrey Wright. His voice, the speech patterns, the timbre of the sound of everything. It was pretty wild.

Were there storylines from the previous films that you felt you could plant Easter eggs for? I’m thinking specifically of the romantic chemistry between Effie and Haymitch.

There are certain Capitol characters where I give a lot of freedom for improvisation. Effie, Caesar, Drusilla [played by Glenn Close], there’s a lot of room for ad-libs. One of the elements that we definitely played with a bit came from an improvised moment in the [last] Mockingjay. We were shooting this scene in Atlanta outside of Snow’s mansion, which is one of the very last scenes of Katniss in the Capitol. She’s saying goodbye to Effie, and then Haymitch and Effie kiss.

Quite honestly, it was an idea because Woody just wanted to kiss Elizabeth Banks. But everybody thought it would be fun and that the fans would dig it, that Haymitch kissed her. Then it became this big thing of this hidden love that Haymitch and Effie have for one another. And Elle played into that a bit. So there’s, I would say, a hint of flirtation here between the two, less so on Haymitch’s side. His heart is obviously somewhere else in the story. But Elle definitely brought a bit of that to it. That was not scripted. That’s the fun of having great actors.

What was it like to reunite Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, and Woody Harrelson from the original movies?

Jen and I have stayed close over the years. We’ve done four movies together. Josh, who basically has moved to Spain, I haven’t seen in a long time. Woody I see off and on and text every once in a while. But there was something really special about the three of them being back together.

It’s also really, for the most part, the same crew from 2012, when we started making Catching Fire. It’s the same DP [Jo Willems], the same camera operator [David J. Thompson], the same AD [Christopher Surgent].

[When] they got to the hotel, Jen and Josh were in the bar having a beer or something, and I was like, Okay, I won’t even shower. I won’t get out of my rain gear. I’ll just come in. The next thing you know, there were 40 of us who had been together since Catching Fire, the gang back together. It’s like a high school reunion or something, but in the best possible way.

There’s a futility to what happens in this film, knowing where we end up in future movies. How do you handle that aspect of history being doomed to repeat itself?

Look, we’re doing a story where you know the lead character is going to make it out. It’s really about how he makes it out, and what he ends up being like at the end of it all. What I’m really pleased about is that the way Suzanne wrote the book, and the way I think we’ve ended the movie, there is a sense of hope that the tragedy is not for nothing. That was really important to me. And one of the beautiful elements in the story, which comes a bit later, is this sense of, everybody has to find their voice. Everybody has to participate.

It really deals with this thing that I think is happening a lot today, where you find apathy: people not wanting to vote, feeling even if they do vote that it’s not going to matter. This idea that you have to be active, and you can’t expect immediate gratification—that everybody needs to stand up and it may take generations, but you still have to do it.

Outside of my screening on the Upper West Side, there was a group protesting Elon Musk and data centers because the documentary about him was playing at the theater. It was a reminder that there will always be something to rise up against, and always people who will be willing to do it.

Yeah, exactly. And ideally, at some point, if everybody stands up, something will change.

During the 13 years that you’ve worked in this universe, dystopia has felt more and more familiar. How have real-world events influenced your filmmaking?

In the 56 years I’ve been alive, there’s never really been a time where I’ve felt like, Oh wow, everything is great. Nothing is wrong in the world. It always feels like there’s some dystopian sense about the world at any given time. And somehow Suzanne is always able to write these stories about it, which is what makes these movies feel timeless. A lot of people just see them as spectacles, but really they’re about our times very specifically. Almost in a subversive way, I feel like we’ve gotten to smuggle these ideas into these movies that a lot of people go see.

#3516. GTA 6 Is Crashing On Some PS5s With CE-108255-1 Error Code

After years of waiting, GTA fans can finally play GTA 6, but some players are encountering a dreaded error code that makes the game crash or otherwise fail.

Users are reporting receiving the CE-108255-1 error code, which players might see when a game crashes mid-session or fails to load entirely. Crashing mid-game in GTA 6 would be particularly frustrating given how saves work.

Sony's official word is that players can try updating their game to fix the issue. If it's really that simple, that would be a welcome result. But people are saying that doesn't always work and are asking Rockstar to put out an official patch.

Reddit user Acrobatic-Promise458 encountered this issue and documented their experience. The person said the game was working normally until they reached a certain point in the story, at which point the game crashes continually. They said Rockstar support directed them to Sony's own support team, but it was no use.

People online (via Gizmodo) are theorizing that the crashing issues with GTA 6 on PS5 might be due to the game's intense demands on the hardware, and it could be specifically tied to older PS5s.

Rockstar has yet to officially respond to these reports. Rockstar's official GTA 6 error troubleshooting page isn't much help, as it only links to the support sites for PlayStation and Xbox and offers no specific help. Players can submit a support ticket to Rockstar to get more help with this issue or others.

These issues do not appear to be very widespread, but if you're experiencing the CE-108255-1 error on PS5, that's no consolation to you.

GTA 6 has reportedly sold 25 million copies and earned more than $2 billion in revenue already, and those numbers are only expected to grow higher.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

#3515. Mary Bonnet Reveals Plans to Move Out of L.A After 'Selling Sunset' Exit

After leaving Selling Sunset, Mary Bonnet revealed she is also planning to move away from Los Angeles.

“We’re likely moving to Nashville,” Mary, 46, told TMZ on Friday, November 20. “The real estate market here is horrible.”

Mary noted that after 25 years in Los Angeles, she was looking for a “more peaceful life.” She also cited her work with animal rescues and how it influenced her lifestyle.

“I’m not good at just sitting idle and although I’m not sitting with the dogs, I need more land because I have a lot of them,” she said. “We’ve had 13 at one point.”

She continued: “I’m starting a rescue of my own. I started off fostering and I started seeing the problems in the system and … once you see it, you can’t unsee it.”

Mary joined Selling Sunset when it premiered in 2019. The reality series became an overnight success for Netflix as viewers were introduced to employees at high-end Los Angeles real estate brokerage The Oppenheim Group.

Earlier this year, Mary shocked viewers when she made the decision to step away ahead of season 10.

“This show actually hurt my real estate business,” she revealed exclusively to Us in July. “I went into Selling Sunset thinking it was going to help — and in the beginning it did.”

The reality star admitted she struggled in her career, adding, “It hasn’t hurt Jason [Oppenheim], but he’s removed from all the drama. Anything they did — even though I was removed from it — still impacted my career. I lost a lot of clients and I lost a lot of deals because of it.”

Despite taking a break from reality TV, Mary wasn’t ruling out a potential return in the future.

“I know that they are switching up the cast, so I hope that it becomes a more positive show. I really do,” she continued. “Maybe I would go back on it if it were really positive. But it’s still Selling Sunset, so I kind of doubt [that]. They’ve said that it’s going to be more positive and about fun for the last three seasons.”

She concluded: “I’ll watch [season 10], but for right now, I don’t want to have any involvement in all of that. It was an amazing run and I’m so grateful for it. But I’m needed in other places right now — and in other ways — between the market and the show and how everything changed. I have this time, so I’m using it for something good.”

Selling Sunset premieres on Netflix December 4.

#3514. GTA 6’s Astonishing $4 Billion Day One Includes 32.5 Million Copies Sold

GTA 6 is an enormous hit--it's the biggest gaming release ever. Take-Two just announced that GTA 6 reach 32.5 million copies sold before release, with revenue reaching $3.79 billion through the end of the first day on sale on November 19. This makes it the biggest entertainment release--for any medium--in history, Take-Two said.

For comparison, 2013's GTA 5 hit $800 million in revenue in its first 24 hours and $1 billion after its first three days, so GTA 6 is pacing well ahead of those numbers. GTA 5 launched at $60, compared to $80 for the cheapest version of GTA 6.

For comparison, the all-time highest-grossing movie ever is Avengers: Endgame, which made $2.94 billion during its entire run. GTA 6 has done nearly $1 billion more in revenue already. According to reporter Jason Schreier, GTA 6 is also now instantly one of the top 30 best-selling games of all time.

“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games
with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser said. “We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”

Big numbers for GTA 6 were always expected. Sensor Tower had been sharing unofficial sales data for GTA 6 for a long time already, but Take-Two's sales numbers are even higher than the 25 million sales that Sensor Tower reported at launch.

GTA 6 is only going to get bigger when it comes to sales as more and more people buy the game. Additionally, GTA 6 is expected to come to PC in 2027, which will be another selling cycle for the game. Beyond this, GTA 6 is expected to add an online mode in 2027 that will no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways for Rockstar to make money off the fanbase.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

#3513. GTA 6 Sets Even More Records

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand. GTA 6 sold more than 30 million copies and hit almost $4 billion on day one, but that's just the start of understanding the impact of the game's release.

For starters, the internet service provider Comcast announced that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the company's history in terms of demand. Peak traffic was 31% higher than an average day and a full 9.6% higher that the previous biggest day ever for traffic to Comcast's network.

GTA 6 also now holds five of the top 10 busiest days of Comcast's network of all time. Going further, Comcast said around 24% of all internet traffic on Comcast's network was people downloading or playing GTA 6 on November 18 (no doubt thanks to the New Zealand trick). Additionally, traffic to Twitch on Comcast's network was up by almost 50% and "is still increasing," Comcast said.

A spokesperson for Comcast further contextualized the traffic data, telling GameSpot that between when preloading began on November 10 and through November 18, PlayStation and Xbox traffic pushed enough data on the network for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K repeatedly for two days straight.

Comcast was among the internet service providers that offered free speed boosts to subscribers to help them download GTA 6 faster.

Additionally, Mat Piscatella of Circana shared data that speaks to the enormity of GTA 6's launch on PlayStation and Xbox. For active accounts November 19 in the US, 61% of PS5 accounts "engaged with" GTA 6. On Xbox, 56% of Xbox players globally did. PS5 players averaged 513 minutes of play for GTA 6 on November 19, compared to 494 on Xbox.

These daily active user and minutes played figures are "absolutely bonkers," Piscatella said. GTA 6 was No. 1 on November 19, pushing Fortnite down to No. 2 based on these engagement metrics, Circana said.

#3512. How to Watch the 'DWTS' Season 35 Finale After Surprise Episode Change

Dancing With the Stars is wrapping up season 35 with its upcoming finale — and fans can expect a major scheduling change.

ABC announced during the semifinals that the season finale will air live in every U.S. time zone for the first time in the show’s history. The three-hour special will premiere Tuesday, November 24, at 8 p.m. ET and 5 p.m. PT.

The finale will air on ABC while streaming live on Disney+. It will re-air at 8:00 p.m. PT and stream the next day on Hulu. Viewers across every coast can watch and vote live as the final five couples — Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik, Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach, Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov, Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas and Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold — compete for the mirrorball trophy.

Each pair will perform three routines: a judges’ choice dance, the instant dance challenge and a freestyle.

The finale comes after Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson were sent home in the semifinals despite receiving perfect scores for both of their dances that night.

“Sometimes when people are doing so well in the competition, people don’t necessarily vote,” cohost Julianne Hough told the duo after they were eliminated. “Because they think you’re doing so well with scores.”

Johnson, 32, later addressed the shocking result while speaking to Us on Wednesday, November 18.

“You know what? It’s very bittersweet,” Johnson said. “I think this season — you never know what’s going to happen, I think we’ve seen that from the very beginning. It’s so exciting that it’s so celebrated. Everyone’s getting to watch dance, but you never know what’s going to happen, and so last night, obviously, I think I was just like a little taken back. But I am so incredibly grateful for my relationship and partnership with Harry, and that goes far beyond these just three months of Dancing With the Stars.”

Johnson shared that she would “cherish” her connection with Shum, 44, “forever.”

“That far outweighs any of the heartache I’m feeling right now of not being in the finals and getting to do a freestyle,” she added.

One week before Johnson and Shum’s exit, Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy‘s elimination took fans by surprise. (Chmerkovskiy, 40, made headlines earlier in the season when he was benched from the show for controversial comments directed toward judge Carrie Ann Inaba.)

“Every week is a shocker,” Chmerkovskiy told Extra after what became his and Dewan’s final performance. “It’s very competitive. A lot of great couples out there. Wishing everybody the best, and I’m gonna be rooting from home. I thought we had a great season.”

Dancing With the Stars’ season 35 finale airs live coast-to-coast on ABC Tuesday, November 24, at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT.

Rocky has returned to the big screen amid the 2026 movie schedule, but not in the way fans of the fictional boxer would’ve likely expected. Sylvester Stallone’s journey to getting the iconic 1976 film made is chronicled in the acclaimed biopic, I Play Rocky, which is helmed by Peter Farrelly. While Stallone had no direct involvement in the movie, he did give it his official stamp of approval to the creative team. However, the beloved actor accidentally sparked some serious drama after the movie was announced, and I was totally unaware of it.

As awards season heats up, the cast and creative team behind I Play Rocky have been making the rounds and promoting the movie. Farrelly recently took part in a wide-ranging discussion with Deadline as part of its Contenders series and reflected on making his latest flick. During the discussion, the Dumb and Dumber helmer spoke about receiving input from Stallone early on about his approach to his family, including his father, Frank Stallone Sr. Also, Sly and Farrelly agreed on a key detail that led the latter to make a request:

There’s a funny story. So, after he signed off, I said — we had the discussion [of] should he come on as a producer. I said, ‘Personally, I think you should not. I think it’s going to hurt you. Because you come across so great [in the film] and, at the end of the movie, if they see ‘executive-produced by Sylvester Stallone’ they’re going to think you shaped it,’ which he didn’t. And he agreed with that, and I said, ‘Just separate yourself a little from this.’

Honestly, the Oscar-winning filmmaker’s rationale (as shared on X) makes a lot of sense. If Stallone were credited as a producer on the film, which shows him in a mostly positive light, many may be tempted to think he manipulated the narrative. The Rambo star is, of course, no stranger to moviemaking so, given his directing and producing experience, I can see why he’d agree. Despite coming to an accord on Stallone needing to “separate” himself from the production, that apparently led to a serious faux pas on the actor’s part:

A week later, he’s doing an interview, and a guy says, ‘What do you think about this movie about the making of Rocky?’ And he goes, ‘I know nothing about it.’ And the internet goes crazy…. [People are like,] ‘These motherfuckers, they’re doing this movie without even going to Sylvester Stallone. Frank Stallone is threatening our lives, [Sly’s] brother. And Frank is like, ‘Can you believe these blah blah blah blah blah.’

The mere thought of getting heat from fans is daunting enough, but receiving heat from a member of the Stallone family is something else entirely. Farrelly went on to say that he later had another chat with the purveyor and lover of the Rocky films, and it went down as follows:

I called Sylvester [and] I go, ‘What are you doing?!’ He goes, ‘What?’ I said, ‘You said you knew nothing about it.’ He goes, ‘You said to separate myself.’ [I said,] ‘Not that far.’ And he says, ‘Oh okay, I will remember that going forward.’

I Thought Rocky And Creed's Big Fight Scene Would Be The End Of I Play Rocky. So What Happened?

While all this drama was due to a simple misunderstanding, it definitely created quite a mess for the filmmaking team. No lasting damage was seemingly done, though, and I’d say that things have been working out for Farrelly and his collaborators. The movie has been well received and gaining considerable buzz in the lead-up to the Oscars. It even received a stamp of approval from Ryan Gosling. As for Stallone, he admitted he was prepared to be “hypercritical” of the film, but he ended up really enjoying the movie as a whole and lead actor Anthony Ippolito’s portrayal of him.

I’d say that’s a generally happy ending to this story in the aftermath of the unintentional drama. Something I appreciate, though, is that Peter Farrelly is far enough removed from the situation that he can joke about it now. What isn’t a laughing matter, though, is the amount of heart that’s present in I Play Rocky, and fans can check out the film in theaters now.
