#3502. Why Kate Middleton's Return to William's Side Says a Lot About the Future of the Monarchy

After days of rumors circulating about Kate Middleton’s possible participation in the trip to India, confirmation came only at the last minute. This news came as a surprise in many ways, even though the princess’s presence was expected. Her involvement in this tour of India deserves attention, especially in light of the increasingly important role she plays alongside Prince William, who will be king. The trip to India, significant in its own right, also included an important meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, aimed at strengthening relations between the United Kingdom and India. This high-profile diplomatic meeting was added after it was confirmed that Modi would return in time from his trip to the Philippines.

The Prince and Princess of Wales arrive at the Earthshot ceremony

Kate’s participation in the royal tour was made official by Kensington Palace only the day before departure to allow the princess to assess her condition right up until the last minute and determine whether she could handle such a demanding trip, following her recovery. But once she arrived in Mumbai, Catherine proved she was ready to do more than initially planned. The princess appeared, as always, impeccable and smiling—perhaps even more so than usual—in her customary understated and polished style. She greeted the crowd and met with people who had come to see her, participating in events alongside her husband.

From the first day of this three-day tour—which began on the anniversary of their official engagement— Kate immediately displayed her characteristic good-natured spirit, evident in past tours as well, by joining Prince William in a game of gully cricket—a street version of the sport—alongside local children and teenagers. Serving as host was Sachin Tendulkar, an Indian sports legend whom the couple had already met during their previous visit to the country in 2016. The two princes put their skills to the test with little formality. They then took a ride on the Mumbai metro—a scene we’d already seen in London in candid photos when the Princess of Wales traveled on a bus in celebration of London Poppy Day.

The Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony

The highlight was the awards ceremony in Mumbai on the evening of the second day, when the Princess of Wales unexpectedly took the stage to deliver a speech dedicated to the power of nature, health, and healing. Her speech was kept secret until the last moment, so much so that not even the celebrities and other guests in attendance knew the Princess of Wales would be speaking. “Nature is precious,” the princess said. “We are not separate from it. We are part of it, deeply connected in ways both visible and unseen…the health of the planet and our natural world is inseparable from our own, and when it thrives, so do we,” she continued. “I have seen firsthand how nature has the power to heal and enrich our daily lives, but so much remains under threat.” “There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time."

Catherine then presented the award in the “Protect and Restore Nature” category, dedicated to the protection and restoration of ecosystems. “The people we’re celebrating tonight are a huge part of that story. Their work will inspire and create seismic change that will improve lives for generations to come,” she said.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony

Over the past three days, William and Kate have been busy meeting about sustainability, innovation, transportation, culture, and relations between the two countries. William is, in fact, assuming an increasingly prominent role on the international stage, supporting the United Kingdom’s diplomatic relations through his travels, which Middleton’s presence reinforced. This time, however, it was not simply a princess accompanying her husband on an official visit, but a woman who, after her illness and a long hiatus from major trips abroad, chose to return to her rightful role—and one the public has long expected her to fill.

The Prince and Princess of Wales with some Earthshot Prize winners

It’s worth noting that this is the first time in four years—since her illness—that Kate has accompanied Prince William on an official overseas mission. The last such occasion was in December 2022, when the couple traveled to Boston, Massachusetts, for the Earthshot Prize ceremony. Her participation in the trip to India thus reflects her desire to gradually resume her international role, as well as her awareness of just how important her presence is to the monarchy.

After her cancer diagnosis in 2024, Catherine prioritized her health and family, returning to public engagements without rushing things. However, her trip to Reggio Emilia, Italy, last May marked an important first step. On that occasion, she appeared visibly engaged and enthusiastic, and in subsequent statements, she hinted at her desire to travel more and gradually resume international engagements. “So I’m so glad it went well for her. I think she came back buzzing.” William said, describing his wife’s mood after that trip. Court circles had also hinted that Catherine wished to gradually resume a more active schedule.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony

Her return to work, however, was approached gradually, respecting the time needed for her recovery. It’s a journey that Kate herself described with great sincerity in a recent interview published last week in Country Life, a magazine for which Prince William served as guest editor. “I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear. There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time,” the princess said, emphasizing that recovery does not necessarily proceed in a steady and predictable manner. India, therefore, did not come as a complete surprise. Rather, it was the realization of a desire that Middleton had already begun to express, and that the princess agreed to undertake such a demanding trip shows she felt ready to take the next step.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in India

Before the trip, Kensington Palace issued a statement emphasizing how much the princess cares about her husband’s environmental initiative and how meaningful it was for her to return to participate in the ceremony in person. “She’s enormously proud of what he’s achieved, and it has been particularly special for them to experience this moment together. They are very much a team.”

This refers to the project’s growth; since her last participation in Boston in 2022, it has significantly expanded its international reach and the impact of the initiatives it supports. “This year’s program in Mumbai promises to be the biggest and most ambitious yet, and she’s excited to see first-hand just how far some of it has come and meet some of the extraordinary people behind that success.” The spokesperson then recalled the couple’s previous trip to India in 2016, explaining that both have particularly fond memories of that visit. “The prince and princess are both really looking forward to what promises to be a fantastic week in India. They have such fond memories of their last visit together in 2016, and are excited to be returning a decade later.”

As mentioned, the most important diplomatic event of the tour took place on November 18 in New Delhi, where Prince William and Kate met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This was the only occasion during the visit when the royal couple left Mumbai, the city that hosted most of their scheduled engagements. Modi returned to the Indian capital specifically for this occasion after attending a major international summit in Manila, Philippines, to take part in the bilateral talks.

A spokesperson for Kensington Palace had emphasized the strategic importance of relations between the two countries, characterized by deep and ever-growing ties in numerous sectors, which include trade, investment, defense, security, technology, education, and culture. Kate’s presence alongside William during the meeting was considered particularly significant. “This meeting reflects the importance of that relationship, as well as the role their royal highnesses can play in celebrating and strengthening the ties between our two countries.”

“For the prince, it also represents another significant engagement as he continues to take on a growing role on the international stage. We’ve seen him increasingly support the UK’s diplomatic relationships through his overseas engagements, and this meeting will provide an opportunity to build on those connections at the highest level.”

India, after all, holds a special place in the history of relations between the British monarchy and the Commonwealth. King Charles has visited the country numerous times, on both official and private occasions, strengthening a personal and institutional relationship over the years. For William and Catherine, however, this trip represented an opportunity to build a direct relationship with a nation destined to play an increasingly important role in the international balance of power.

A close-up of the Prince and Princess of Wales

With a population of over 1.4 billion people, India is now the world’s most populous country and one of the fastest-growing economies. Hosting the Earthshot Prize meant engaging a potentially massive audience on issues of environmental sustainability, resource conservation, and innovative solutions to combat climate change.

A beautiful image of the Prince and Princess of Wales

For William and Kate, returning to India also meant revisiting a country to which they are bound by personal memories. As mentioned, their last visit was in April 2016, when the Prince and Princess of Wales—then the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge—undertook an official tour of India and Bhutan at the request of the British government. During that trip, they visited Mumbai, met with representatives from India’s cultural and sports communities, and traveled to Agra, where they admired the Taj Mahal.

Right in front of the famous mausoleum—a symbol of eternal love—William and Kate sat on the same white marble bench where, 24 years earlier, Lady Diana, Princess of Wales, posed during a visit to India. That photograph of Diana, portrayed alone in front of the monument, became one of the most iconic images of her public life. Taken in 1992, when her marriage to Charles was going through a deep crisis, many interpreted it as a visual representation of her loneliness. In 2016, William and Kate’s decision to recreate that shot inevitably brought Diana to mind, adding a personal and symbolic dimension to their visit.

For Catherine, therefore, this trip is above all a new step on her journey back to public life following her illness. Not a demonstration of recovery to be celebrated as a race against time, but an opportunity to resume playing an important role while moving at her own pace. And to stand once again alongside William on a mission that concerns not only the future of the monarchy, but also that of the planet.

Originally published by Vanity Fair Italy.

Warning! The following contains spoilers from the 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way episode "The Parent Trapped." Stream the episode with an HBO Max subscription, or read at your own risk!

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way brought back Kenny Niedermeier and Armando Rubio, but this wasn't the happy reunion fans might've wanted. Their journey on the 2026 TV schedule kicked off by highlighting a medical emergency with Armando's daughter, Hannah. With that, Armando has since provided an update on the situation.

The 90 Day franchise's most wholesome couple was blindsided by a mysterious illness, which saw Hannah experience a brain bleed. As a result, she needed to be airlifted from Mexico to receive advanced medical care in the United States. The episode showed Kenny meeting her at the hospital, while Armando worked to obtain a visa to try to be with her. Fortunately, she's doing much better in the present day, and as fate would have it, Rubio shared that today is her fourteenth birthday:

A post shared by Armando Niedermeier-Rubio (@armando_90day)

If you're someone who follows Kenny or Armando on social media, so much of this storyline has already been divulged. For example, Hannah has recovered, and while there still isn't a public reason why her brain bleed happened, she appears to be doing very well. As a result of her recovery, she was also able to return to Mexico.

90 Day Fiancé’s David Dangerfield Spoke Out After Former Fiancé Sheila Mangubat Died

As for Armando, he was able to obtain an emergency visa to get to the United States to be with Hannah, thanks to some work by Congresswoman Adelita Grijalva. So, for anyone watching the latest episode and holding their breath waiting for some bad news, you can breathe easy now.

Overall, it's been pretty upsetting to watch this unfold on TV, back when Kenny and Armando had no idea how it was going to play out. It's a rare moment where 90 Day Fiancé chooses to roll with an event as it unfolds, despite it clearly not being what they planned to cover from the start.

Fortunately, this was a story with a happy ending, which was not guaranteed. My heart hurt for Kenny when he said he saw Hannah for the first time after she'd been admitted to the hospital in the United States and she looked unsure of who he was. For him, as a parent, that had to be heartbreaking to witness, but it seemed like he was able to put on a brave face for Armando.

Fans of 90 Day surely know that Hannah is Armando's world and was his daughter from his marriage before he met Kenny. They've lived together happily in Mexico, with Kenny, who moved away from his previous family (as seen in The Other Way Season 2) before joining them.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way continues on TLC on Sundays at 8:00 p.m. ET. This season is full of majors moments, and while we don't know how many of them will play out, I'm happy that we know Hannah is doing better.

#3500. GTA 6 Is Approaching An Absurd New Sales Milestone, Report Says

Grand Theft Auto 6's success continues to come into focus, as a new report from Alinea Analytics says the game sold 44.9 million copies through its first weekend. This would be up from the 32.5 million copies that Rockstar owner Take-Two announced last week, covering the game's pre-purchases alone.

According to Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics, GTA 6 has reached 33.7 million copies sold on PS5 and 11.2 million on Xbox Series X|S, for a split of 75.1% to 24.9%.

Take-Two announced $3.79 billion in sales for GTA 6 on day one, and Alinea estimated that the figure has grown to $4 billion through its first four days.

Sony and Microsoft keep 30% of the revenue for digital copies via platform fees, so those companies are winners here as well.

Elliott went on to point out that GTA 6's $4 billion in revenue thus far is roughly equal to the combined box office results for this year's two biggest movies, Spider-Man: Brand New Day ($2.5 billion) and The Odyssey ($1.8 billion). Of course, GTA 6 is an $80-$100 game, while (hopefully) no one is spending that much to see a movie, at least not at one time.

Elliott also shared data that shows around 40.8 million people logged in to play GTA 6 on Sunday, November 22, with PS5 making up 76% of those players. Additionally, Elliott said the data shows that about 20% of players--or about 9 million people--have spent more than 20 hours in the game already.

GTA 6 is only going to get bigger when it comes to sales as more and more people buy the game. Additionally, GTA 6 is expected to come to PC in 2027, which will be another selling cycle for the game. Beyond this, GTA 6 is expected to add an online mode in 2027 that will no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways for Rockstar to make money off the fanbase.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

#3499. Inside Chris Brown and Usher's 'Tension' on Tour: 'Egos Started to Show'

The R&B Tour has been anything but smooth sailing for Chris Brown and Usher behind the scenes.

“There has been tension between Chris and Usher throughout the tour,” a source exclusively tells Us. “Their teams tried to keep it under lock and key, but everyone knew it was only a matter of time until it became public.”

Brown, 37, and Usher, 48, kicked off The R&B Tour at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver on June 26. The tour — featuring supporting acts Tank, Mario and Eric Bellinger — was initially considered a success, expanding from 33 to 59 dates due to fan demand and grossing $77.4 million in September alone, according to Billboard Boxscore.

However, rumors of a feud between Brown and Usher quickly spread on social media after they began their November 5 show at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta approximately two and a half hours late. TMZ subsequently reported that the coheadliners had gotten into an argument backstage, delaying their usual start time for their 50-plus-song set. Brown and Usher have since canceled concerts at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on November 16 and Hard Rock Stadium in Miami on December 6 without offering an explanation to ticket holders.

“Chris and Usher have worked together a few times over the years, but they never had a genuine brothership beyond that,” the insider explains to Us. “It was more of a professional respect for each other’s artistry than anything else. Planning and executing this tour forced them to spend more time together, and eventually their egos started to show and they clashed.”

Despite their lingering beef and two scrapped performances, Brown and Usher appear to be forging on with the remainder of The R&B Tour, which is currently scheduled to conclude with back-to-back nights at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida, on December 11 and 2. In fact, the “New Flame” collaborators have continued to put on a united front on stage, even hugging it out during a separate Atlanta concert on November 10.

“One thing they can agree on is that they want to finish out the tour because the fan response has been amazing and they still have a few surprises up their sleeves that have been in the works for a while,” the source tells Us. “Their teams remain hopeful that can happen, but it won’t be easy.”

Us has reached out to reps for Brown and Usher for comment.

Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage has been in more than a few seasoned actors during its run. Now, for Season 3, the producers have recruited a veteran from one of the best sitcoms of all time, and I couldn't be happier with this casting decision. Cheers actor John Ratzenberger will join the fun in an upcoming episode amid the 2026 TV schedule, and I'm hoping the door is open for future appearances.

According to TV Insider, Ratzenberger will join the CBS series during its December 10th episode, which will air on the network and be available to those with a Paramount+ subscription on streaming. Known for his role as mailman Cliff Clavlin on Cheers, Ratzenberger plays a World War II veteran named Davey, who crosses paths with Jim McAllister (Will Sasso) when he attends a community bingo night. Here's what Ratzenberger had to say about it:

[Jim] and his bride come in, and they’re uncomfortable at first because there’s a bunch of old people in there, but eventually they warm up to it, they understand the meaning of it.

It sounds like a great episode for Jim and Audrey, who have struggled to come to grips with aging in the past couple of seasons. Jim selling his tire shop to Georgie allowed him to retire, but it has now left him with a lot of spare time on his hands that he doesn't know how to fill. Could this bingo night become a new tradition for him and Audrey?

Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage Just Avoided Another Disaster, And I'm Curious What It'll Take For Them To Split

A friendship with Davey and other people at the bingo hall could help them increase their social circle and make some friends with some people older than them. Jim and Audrey aren't quite senior citizens just yet, but with all their free time, it wouldn't hurt to get some advice from their elders on how to best spend the spare time they have on their hands.

With all the guest stars coming to Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage, the question still lingers as to whether Iain Armitage will reprise his role as Sheldon Cooper this season. This comes after recent reports that there was an offer for him to return in the first season, but Armitage ultimately declined.

The good news is the show isn't struggling to find talented guest stars elsewhere, as I'm sure people will be happy to see John Ratzenberger. It'll be great to see him doing something in addition appearing in a Pixar movie, and he seems plenty amped up about the role. There's also a personal layer to this casting, as Ratzenberger mentioned that his father was a veteran. With that, he was eager to take on this new role.

As far as what's on the way for Georgie & Mandy, that's an excellent question. The titular couple hasn't had a lot of issues this season, though there's seemingly going to be some offer where Mandy can take a job outside of Medford. We've known for a while that Georgie isn't down for that idea, so I'll be curious to see what he has to say.

Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage continues on CBS on Thursdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. Season 3 is a joy to watch so far, and I don't expect that to change anytime soon! Be sure to stream the show on Paramount+ as well, and know that with that same subscription, you can stream John Ratzenberger's work on Cheers.

#3497. Somehow, Jensen Huang Returned

Nvidia has announced that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as president and CEO of Nvidia, while he'll also return to the Board of Directors. This is happening just hours after US President Donald Trump said Huang should come back.

"The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia," the technology giant said. "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

Nvidia chair of the Board Harvey C. Jones said the Board believes "Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers."

"We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's Chief Financial Officer," he added.

Trump said in a social media post that Nvidia's Board made "the correct and proper decision" to bring Huang back. Trump went on to say that the US government has no real to believe that Huang's return "poses any risk to national security."

For his part, Huang said he is honored to return to Nvidia to lead what he called "one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution."

"I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Huang was ousted from Nvidia earlier this month after it came to light that he had a romantic relationship with a person that sources said was possibly a spy for China, though no hard evidence was ever provided to back this up. It was later reported that Huang had multiple other affairs with people he worked with.

In response to the reports, Nvidia formed a committee made up of independent directors who had the job of investigating the "foreign intelligence" claims. Additionally, the committee hired an independent attorney to assist, and that investigation remains ongoing, with Huang's support. In addition to the internal investigation, there are multiple other open cases against Nvidia, including a probe by the SEC over financial accounting claims.

In response to the entire situation, Nvidia has also created a new National Security and Export Control Committee to "oversee trade complicance and national security risks."

Prior to today, Nvidia's board said it had no intention of bringing Huang back, but things can change fast. For his part, Huang said he would be "honored" to return as Nvidia's CEO.

The Nvidia controversies led to turmoil in the stock market, in part because Nvidia is one of the “Mag 7” companies that are driving growth in the US. Some of the information coming to light suggests that Nvidia’s accounting and export control compliance are not buttoned up, and this has fueled further concerns about the growth potential and returns on investment for the AI trade.

Numerous other technology and AI stocks have dropped in value significantly since the Nvidia news broke. Now that Huang is back as CEO, though, not only is Nvidia's stock price ripping, but the market overall--not just AI and tech stocks--is seeing positive upwards trends.

#3496. Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

The iPhone Duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first. Personally, I’ve had my eye on the Google variant, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold—and recently I finally took the plunge. I thought I’d done my research to know how different having a foldable phone would be, but I still had a bit to learn. Here are some of the things I wish I’ve learned along the way after making the jump to foldables.

One of the most notable aspects of the iPhone Duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed. And there’s a good reason for that: The larger screen while open has exactly the same 1.41:1 aspect ratio as the smaller screen while closed. This has a ripple effect on how every app you use looks and feels—and whether you like Apple’s approach is largely a matter of personal preference.

Compare with my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which features an extremely tall 2.17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open. On the outer screen, apps are a little less wide than on my old phone, but there’s plenty of space for reading books or articles on the inner screen.

I like the tall, thin display personally because it feels easier to reach buttons with my thumb, and the wider display is better for reading. However, this approach can occasionally result in some odd app layouts. Not every app is designed for tablets, especially on Android, and shifting the aspect ratio between the inner and outer display sometimes means re-rendering or even restarting an app entirely to load properly.

The iPhone Duo has a more consistent aspect ratio and general feel between the inner and outer display, but it comes at the cost of a really wide phone. Neither approach is better or worse on its own, but it might be worth going to a local store to get your hands on the phone you’re thinking about before buying.

For years, the screens on most smartphones have been made of increasingly tough and scratch-resistant glass. So tough that you might not even need a screen protector anymore. On a foldable phone, that can be true of the outside display, but it’s very much not when it comes to the inner, foldable display.

Screens might be foldable, but the strong, durable glass that makes your phone so scratch-resistant isn’t. No matter what foldable phone you use, the covering on the inner display will be more flexible, and thus softer. Apple uses a nano-texture polymer film that can be replaced, but the film on most foldable phones cannot. That means if they get damaged or scratched, those marks will be there for the life of your phone.

If you (like me) haven’t considered a screen protector in a while, it might be time to try one again, at least for the inner display. It’s also worth keeping in mind how rough you plan to be with your phone. Construction sites or factories might not be the best home for a foldable phone you plan to open a lot, but an office job should be a bit safer.

Similar to the screen protector issue, cases can be more of a headache. Most rigid cases will come in two pieces, and the piece that covers the outer display can be shockingly minimal—barely more than a frame, for some of the cases I looked at. A poorly made case can be brittle or pop off more easily, so it’s more important to get a high-quality one.

If you like to use your phone case as your wallet, it’s also important to be wary of cases that aren’t specifically designed for your model of phone (and maybe some that are). A lot of wallet cases are built to unfold to reveal your phone’s screen on one side, and your cards and ID on the other. But depending on how your foldable phone unfolds, it could be awkward to reach the inner screen.

The hinge also introduces more spaces for dust and debris to get into your phone. Despite the extra moving parts and gaps, most foldable phones still offer the now-standard IP68 dust and water resistance rating. That mainly applies to what can get inside and damage the components inside your phone. It’s still possible for hair and dirt to get gummed up in any pinchable spaces, so look out for any case that might provide even more nooks for dust to collect in.

I’ve set up most of my apps how I like them by now, but when I first got my foldable phone, I had to revisit some settings I thought I was done messing with. One of the most notable examples was my ebook apps: I was previously using a single-column, medium-font layout, but it looked ridiculous on the inner display. After switching to a two-column layout, it not only felt more natural, but a lot like reading a regular book.

Similarly, there were some uses for my calendar app that got a whole lot more useful. I’ve never really been able to use anything other than either the one-day or Schedule view if I want to make out anything, but on the inner screen, I can finally look at my week at a glance. But that meant tweaking some things—like showing reminders, which fit naturally amid my events in Schedule view, but become a cluttered mess when I saw 14 different reminders to take my meds at once in the Week view.

Most apps do a decent job of automatically adjusting to different screen sizes, but I found a few outliers that I had to figure out myself. As an example, Google Docs would default to a view with extremely tiny text when I first started using it. It took me a bit to figure out that this was due to a “Print layout” toggle in the document’s settings. This is, for some reason, enabled by default when opening a document on the larger inner screen. It can take some time to learn the eccentricities of all your apps, but it’s worth poking around when you can.

I know, it sounds so obvious, right? The outer screen is the one you’ll use most often, so how could you forget about it? But when you unfold the inner screen, the outer one is still useful in some surprising ways that I hadn’t even considered until I went poking around in some of my apps.

One of the most adorable examples is the Made You Look feature in the Pixel’s Camera app. When unfolded, you can take a picture using the rear camera and see a preview like normal, while the outer screen shows silly animations to capture the attention of a baby or toddler that you want to look into the camera. Admittedly, this is an older feature, but it’s a clever one. For adults, you can also use the outer display to get a selfie preview while using the rear-facing camera.

The outer screen is also just better for some things. YouTube is one of the few apps that has a unique layout designed for a partially folded screen, with the video playing on the tilted-up portion of the screen, and video controls on the bottom portion.

However, in my experience, it was a lot nicer to watch a YouTube video by just propping up the outer screen by unfolding the phone a bit, like a kickstand. My Pixel even detected when YouTube was in full-screen mode on the outer display and would be more forgiving of unfolding the phone without switching to the inner screen. The phone anticipated I might just want to prop up the smaller screen, which I thought was a nice touch.

#3495. Christmas in July? Why Stop There?

Why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays? The fact that Thanksgiving and Christmas are just four weeks apart means by the time you’ve returned from November family visits, unpacked, shopped, decorated, done the party circuit, bought gifts, and maybe—maybe—worked for a few days, you have to turn around and celebrate again. It’s exhausting and expensive and too warp-speed to feel like that much of a good time. I’m not arguing to ban Christmas—which I am using as a catchall for nondenominational winter holidays, however that looks to you—what I am proposing is, in fact, much more exciting. I think we should switch the dates of Christmas and Valentine’s Day.

Consider it! Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out. Valentine’s Day is for romance, whether that means watching Bridget Jones’s Diary with friends, eating overpriced meals at candlelit restaurants, making cards, or mainlining chocolates. So on December 24, celebrate platonic love with friends—à la Galentine’s Day, except we should think of a better name—and maybe go on a date on the 25th. If that date goes well: bam! You now have a plus-one to a New Year’s Eve party and a midnight make out partner.

If the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season. Life is slow. But by the time everyone trickles back home from watching Die Hard in their pajamas or shopping post-Christmas sales or going to the gym, you only have to survive one month until the sweet relief of spring in late March. Nothing makes more sense for how to survive the long nights and cold of winter.

So we go all-in on spring. Mid-April is when it likely won’t snow again; around then you no longer need heat—at least in New York City—so let’s make that a national holiday celebrating warm weather with seasonal bouquets (tulips, lilacs, peonies), foraged ramps, and maybe specials on dry-cleaning winter coats or sales on shearling boots.

But why stop there? We in America could take a page from France, where May can have four(!) public holidays as a kind of summer practice run. I’d be more than happy to celebrate VE Day in solidarity: Liberté, égalité, holiday! In our version, maybe botanical gardens will be free to the public for picnics. Maybe amusement parks will be gratis? Maybe lobster rolls and strawberry shortcake will be handed out on the street? Can the first summer blockbuster of May be an annual event with free popcorn? This month of long weekends will culminate in Memorial Day barbecues, which is a perfect bookend to summer with Labor Day—no notes.

Let’s keep summer luxurious, so summer Fridays will not be at the discretion of employers but mandated by the government for those three months. The Fourth of July can stay where it is with the caveat that if it rains, we get to observe it on the next day forecast for hot dog weather. Nothing important happens in August—phone it in, federal holiday or not. Labor Day stays, of course. The week following it in New York is Fashion Week, which runs concurrently with the US Open for tennis—very busy but very social. We’re going to adopt that nationwide as a festive season soft launching the country into fall.

And finally, let’s turn our attention to that somber stretch of time between early September and Thanksgiving. We don’t get enough time off, so we will move Presidents’ Day from February to mid-October for another much-needed holiday. Then cook a big turkey dinner on Thanksgiving, see your extended family, watch football, whatever, and delight in the fact that you don’t have to do it again until February. But start figuring out your Valentine’s Day dates now—those prix fixe dinners with chocolate lava cakes really book up fast these days.

#3492. The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

Since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence. But more recently, Black Friday has also metastasized. It's not a day anymore. It's a week, a month, a veritable state of mind. (Speaking of which, check out Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage. We got all the deals, baby!)

While pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a big deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025. But how did Black Friday come about, and what does it all mean?

“Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy. “Black Friday” as a description of the day after Thanksgiving dates back to 1951; the term first appeared in the journal Factory Management and Maintenance, where it referred to the number of employees who skipped work on the day after Thanksgiving. Around the same time, the police in Philadelphia and Rochester started informally using “Black Friday” to describe the traffic and crowds that appeared in their cities as shoppers hit the stores on the day after Thanksgiving. The phrase gradually caught on. It was picked up by national press in 1975 when the New York Times used "Black Friday" specifically to describe the day after Thanksgiving and the shopping and sales it brings.

But even before it had a name, Black Friday was a thing. The day after Thanksgiving has been known by merchants as the start of the shopping season since the late 1800s. By the early 20th century, retailers sponsored Thanksgiving Day parades that traditionally ended with an appearance by Santa Claus, as if to say, “Now it’s time to shop for Christmas.” By unspoken agreement among retailers, Christmas-themed advertisements rarely appeared before Thanksgiving in our grandparents’ day. This informal bargain obviously no longer applies.

Referring to a day as “black” traditionally denotes a period of calamity or tragedy, leading some to suggest different names for the day. In the early 1960s, Philadelphia merchants suggested “Big Friday,” a name which did not catch on, leaving retailers with the weak explanation that the “black” in Black Friday refers to the black ink denoting profits in a ledger. Oft-repeated lore suggests that retailers are "in the red" all year, and only start making an annual profit at the end of the year, but big retail chains generally make money all year long.

A more modern issue with the name is that Black Friday sales now last for days or even weeks, beginning in early to mid-November and bleeding over into the following Saturday, Sunday, “Cyber Monday,” Tuesday, and beyond, leading people to say things like, “Do you want to go Black Friday shopping this Sunday?” So far, alternative names like “Five-Day Frenzy” and “The day I get to trample someone to save $8 on a Nespresso” haven’t caught on. But here’s hoping.

Beginning around 2010, an insatiable thirst for profits led many retailers to push the start of Black Friday shopping to Thursday (aka Thanksgiving Day). Kmart opened Thanksgiving morning. Toys R Us opened that night. By 2011, Walmart was opening its doors at 10 p.m. on Thursday. The trend led to widespread backlash, with many Americans appalled that employees were forced to work on Thanksgiving or angry that consumerism was encroaching upon a holiday meant to celebrate colonialism. By 2021, most major retailers had relented and elected to remain closed on Thanksgiving.

The term “Cyber Monday” describes the boost in online retail sales on the Monday after Thanksgiving, sparked by workers returning to the office and getting right to online shopping. The term first appeared on Nov. 28, 2005, in a Shop.org press release entitled “'Cyber Monday’ Quickly Becoming One of the Biggest Online Shopping Days of the Year," which may be the most influential press release ever written. Since its early 2000s birth, Cyber Monday has become the biggest online shopping day of the year. Americans spent $14.25 billion online on Cyber Monday 2025, according to Adobe Analytics. So is Cyber Monday bigger than Black Friday? Retailers really don't care: Analysts now tend to mash everything into the category of "Black Friday–Cyber Monday" (or even "Cyber Week").

If all this naked consumerism makes you a little squeamish, you're not alone. Anti-consumerists have named the day after Thanksgiving “Buy Nothing Day,” which you can celebrate by doing charity work, cutting up your credit cards, or simply not purchasing anything. Pioneered by artist Ted Dave and popularized by Adbusters magazine, the first Buy Nothing Day was celebrated in Canada in 1992.

It’s hard to measure the success of the alternative holiday. Both online and brick-and-mortar retail sales have increased sharply since 1992, suggesting Buy Nothing Day’s effect is negligible. On the other hand, maybe big retailers are losing millions because someone on Bluesky reminded you not to shop. Sure.

Depending on how you measure it, Black Friday has resulted in between one and 17 deaths. Jdimytai Damour is the only person killed directly due to a Black Friday sale: The 34-year-old worker was trampled to death by a surging crowd at a Long Island Walmart on Black Friday in 2008. If you include car accidents, shootings, retail worker suicides, and fatal heart attacks, Black Friday’s death toll balloons to 17, with 128 reported injuries.

Black Friday violence has even inspired a horror flick: Eli Roth's 2023 holiday-themed slasher Thanksgiving opens with a hilariously brutal Black Friday riot at a big box store, setting off a chain of events that involve a lot of people being murdered by a dude in a Pilgrim mask.

I mean, yeah, of course. Critics of Black Friday point out that there are arguably better times to buy a new TV (like the week before the Super Bowl), not to mention plenty of other goods. Savings from Black Friday shopping are often illusory—big-ticket “doorbuster” items generally sell out quickly, leaving behind goods that are, by and large, priced the same as they would be at any other time of year. Some retailers even mark up products ahead of Black Friday so the discounts look bigger. If you're buying online, your browser history, location, and cart contents can tweak the prices you see on Black Friday, as they can on any other day.

Yet despite protest holidays, the unpleasantness of shopping when stores are overcrowded, and the frustration of hunting for bargains that often aren't that great to begin with, Black Friday stubbornly remains an unofficial holiday, celebrated by over 100 million Americans in one way or another. What that says about our country's relationship with capitalism is unclear, but personally, I’m going to continue my own day-after-Thanksgiving tradition of eating pie for breakfast and thinking about going for a walk, but then watching The Quick and the Dead instead. I'm not protesting anything; I just don't need the hassle.

There’s been a lot of chatter regarding who the next “Bond Girl” might be, and more than a few potential candidates are reportedly being considered. Now, fans have to wonder whether Kim Kardashian is now in the mix due to some recent insider comments.

At this point, Kim Kardashian is far more than a reality TV star at this point. The past few years, in particular, have seen her expand her resume as an actor, as she’s picked up a few high-profile roles. 007 is arguably on a different level, though, and it’s an honor for someone to be cast in one of the films at all, let alone as a Bond Girl. Why Gen Z Is Claiming Robert Pattinson As Their James Bond

Even before Robert Pattinson was cast as Commander Bond earlier this month, the rumor mill had long been churning out potential names for Bond Girls. That chatter has only increased in the aftermath of the Pattinson news. Margaret Qualley is currently leading the prediction markets with others like Anya Taylor-Joy and Florence Pugh also in that ranking. Another star who’s been linked to rumors is Alexandra Daddario, and she recently addressed the chatter by mostly laughing it off as Internet speculation.

There’s no telling when Amazon MGM Studios will announce the next Bond Girl, and I’m eager to see who gets the part. And, regardless of whether Kim Kardashian is the star to get it or not, I can imagine that the pick is going to spark plenty of conversations amongst fans.

#3490. New Hunger Games Movie Blows Past Expectations After Some Feared GTA 6 Could Limit Its Reach

The newest Hunger Games movie, Sunrise on the Reaping, had a gigantic opening weekend that exceeded expectations. Some theorized it could struggle as people stayed home to playGTA 6, which released one day prior, but that doesn't appear to have been the case.

At the domestic box office, Sunrise on the Reaping earned $120 million for its opening weekend, with $105 million more from international markets for a total of $225 million over its first three days, according to Deadline.

The franchise's second prequel, after 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, Sunrise on the Reaping tells the story of the 50th Hunger Games, where Haymitch Abernathy emerged victorious. Joseph Zada plays him; Woody Harrelson played Haymitch in the original Hunger Games films.

Sunrise on the Reaping also stars Ralph Fiennes as a younger President Snow, Jesse Plemons as a younger Plutarch, and Elle Fanning as a younger Effie.

With $120 million for its domestic opening, Sunrise on the Reaping is now just the second prequel film ever to start with $100 million or more domestically. The current top prequel is 2016's Star Wars movie Rogue One, which made $155 million for its domestic opening.

Some had theorized that Sunrise on the Reaping could suffer as people stayed home to play GTA 6 instead. Director Francis Lawrence said, "Hopefully, people find time for both." It sure seems like he was right about that.

For comparison, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes debuted to just $44.6 million for its opening weekend in North America, so Sunrise on the Reaping is doing much better. Sunrise on the Reaping is also Lionsgate's biggest post-COVID movie and its first film that opened to $100 million or more since 2015's The Hunger Games: Mockingjay: Part 2 ($102.6 million).

#3489. 49ers Share Update After Colton McKivitz Suffers Grotesque Injury on ‘SNF'

The San Francisco 49ers issued an update on the status of offensive lineman Colton McKivitz after he was carted off the field following a grotesque ankle injury on Sunday Night Football.

“We think it’s broken and dislocated,” head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the team’s 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday, November 22.

Due to the severity of the injury, McKivitz, 30, will almost assuredly miss the rest of the season.

“That was really crushing,” Shanahan, 46, added. “Colton has had an unbelievable year. … It was tough to see Colton go down like that.”

McKivitz suffered the injury during the game’s second quarter, when his leg and ankle got rolled up during a tackle on a run by teammate Christian McCaffrey. The lineman’s ankle bent at a horrifying angle, which was briefly visible on the NBC broadcast. No further replays were shown.

Players from both teams were noticeably upset, with 49ers left tackle Trent Williams slamming his helmet to the ground.

An air cast was placed on McKivitz’s leg and he was carted to the locker room. No official updates about his condition have been made available.

“It’s brutal,” McCaffrey, 30, said after the game. “He’s somebody that is one of the heart and souls of this team, a guy who shows up every day with the right attitude. He’s the standard, and we’re going to really miss him. We all love him. We’re praying for him.”

The running back added, “It’s one of the worst parts about this game is stuff like that, but we love him and we’re going to play for him from here on out.”

McKivitz was in the midst of his sixth season in the NFL and with the 49ers. He signed a three-year, $45 million contract extension with San Francisco in September 2025, which came after previously being cut by the team in August 2021.

“I don’t want to leave here,” McKivitz said after signing his extension. “Obviously being cut, I’ve got some scars there, but there was a reason why I was drafted here, why I was cut here, and why I still play here.”

He added, “There’s a sense of family. When you have a core group of players who understand a winning culture and understand the standard of what this franchise was built on … it’s hard for guys to turn that away.”

The 49ers return to action when they host the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, November 29.

#3488. Lesley Manville, Pierce Brosnan, and More Celebrate Violinist Joshua Bell at the Langham London

At the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since. “I don’t remember falling in love with music,” says Bell. “Music has just been my life. I used to string rubber bands on my dresser drawers and make pitches by pulling the drawers out. I was fascinated with strings. It’s the closest instrument to the human voice. And I find it the most expressive instrument.”

Today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era. By 14, Bell was performing with the Philadelphia Orchestra, and would soon be touring the world. “I live in hotels 250 days a year,” says Bell of the nonstop schedule he has maintained since his teens. Specifically, Bell has been “staying at the Langham for decades now,” he says, referring to the regal central London hotel that first opened in 1865. “I chose it on my own because it was near one of my favorite halls in London, which is the Wigmore Hall. And now I stay with them whenever I’m traveling.”

That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.

Attendees included actor Simon Callow, House of Dragon actor Emily Carey, former British culture minister Ed Vaizey, Saturday Night Live UK cast producer Susie Hall, stage and television actor Indira Varma, and Verity actor Ismael Cruz Córdova.

Held in partnership with Vanity Fair, the evening marked the latest iteration of the Langham’s Luminaries in Residence program. The event series is continuation of the hotel’s legacy that brings together a diverse, influential community—an evocative reminder of prominent guests from its storied past, including Charles Dickens, Winston Churchill, George Orwell, Oscar Wilde, and Mark Twain.

“I’m not going to put my name in the same sentence as Toscanini or Mark Twain—who has stayed here, or Churchill, who has stayed here. But it’s cool to be part of the history,” says Bell. “So maybe someday, in a hundred years, there will be a violinist who might say that—that I stayed here. I don’t know, maybe that would mean something.”

It certainly does mean something. Pierce Brosnan and his wife, Keely Shaye Brosnan, “have been huge fans of Joshua for many, many years,” Brosnan tells me. “Keely went to go see him…I don’t know how many years back. Unfortunately, due to the LA traffic, she got there late, five minutes late, and they wouldn’t let her into the concert. So tonight is one of those nights.”

Bell, who performed mid-dinner with members of the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields—with a surprise appearance from his wife, soprano Larisa Martínez—brought about a collective catharsis.

Dazzling, fiery, and flamboyant, the experience of watching Bell up close is impossible to replicate. “I just think he’s incredibly soulful, and there’s something really elegant,” actor Russell Tovey tells me, before explaining how he actually discovered Bell via his Instagram algorithm.

For actor Lesley Manville, the event marked her introduction to Bell’s music. “I’m a bit embarrassed that he was not on my radar. But isn’t that nice to have a surprise like that?” says Manville. “Schubert’s String Quintet is one of my favorite pieces of music. It’s unbelievably beautiful. You think of a violin, you think of those strings. And it’s instant emotion. They just make you cry.”

There is a great power in being able to access the emotions of others, as Bell does.

“I think it is the ultimate gift to be able to make people happy,” says Brosnan. “My job is being an entertainer—to take the words of great writing and try to transform it into something that is meaningful and memorable.”

Speaking of entertaining, the week’s announcement that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond was front of mind. “I wish him every joy and every success. He and I made a movie a number of years ago called Remember Me. I played his father. So I was very, very pleased and joyful for his nomination and now his success, and I believe he will be magnificent.”

And that creative full circle is exactly what the night was advocating. “Our own Luminaries in Residence program reflects our belief that meaningful hospitality creates genuine connection with extraordinary talents with one another, and with arts,” Bob van den Oord, CEO of Langham Hospitality Group, explained as he took the stage. “The Langham isn’t simply a place to stay, but a place to gather, exchange ideas, and indeed celebrate.”

The events will take place on three different dates:

Walmart's Black Friday Deals Event 1: Nov. 12–15

Available online and in stores starting at 6 a.m. local time

Online only: Nov. 23 starting at 12:01 a.m. ET

Online and in stores: Nov. 27 starting at 6 a.m. local time

Walmart+ members get six hours of early access online beginning Nov. 23 at 12:01 a.m. ET

Walmart's Cyber Monday Deals Event: Nov. 30-Dec. 2

In short, yes. Though they aren't quite as impactful as they once were, Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales offer discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Whether it's a major purchase you've been saving up for or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts, especially on items like appliances and electronics. Last year's sales included categories such as tech, home improvement, and fitness.

Black Friday used to be when major retailers offered their best deals on expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. #3485. Which Past Characters Would Lindsay Lohan Spend Holidays With?

If Lindsay Lohan could ring in the holiday season with one of her former beloved characters, she has one — or two — from an iconic film in mind.

“The best would be to have the best of both worlds, which would be Hallie and Annie, because then you’d be in London with all those Christmas lights, and then you’d be in Napa in this beautiful vineyard setting,” Lohan, 40, exclusively told Us of her Parent Trap characters while celebrating the launch of her Marshalls Unwrap the Internet partnership.

Lohan famously portrayed long-lost identical twin sisters in the 1998 remake, with Hallie and Annie growing up with their separated parents in Napa Valley, California, and London, respectively. The movie, directed by Nancy Meyers, followed the girls meeting at a summer sleepaway camp before switching places in a ruse to bring their parents (played by Dennis Quaid and the late Natasha Richardson) back together.

“I would definitely choose them because then you get two for one,” Lohan said to Us. “And that’s also like a Nancy Meyers Christmas. So you can’t really say no to that.”

While fans are still holding out hope that Lohan might reprise her Parent Trap roles in the future, they may be appeased by the actress reuniting with Mean Girls director Mark Waters for a new romantic comedy drama.

“I loved working with Mark again,” Lohan told Us of collaborating on the upcoming film Return to You. “You forget how lucky you are when you get to work with a director who knows you because we have done so many films together. And now doing it at this point in my life, at this stage — just our work ethic is so on point and on par and we get things done so quickly in such a great way.”

Lohan gushed that she is confident Return to You, which also stars Henry Golding, is going to be fantastic” because Waters is “such a great director.”

“It was a bit nostalgic because I was there alone,” she said of filming in Toronto. “So to go there with my family now is really exciting, and for Halloween it was really cute. My son really enjoyed it. We shot at the old Mean Girls house. We ate at some of the same restaurants that I had eaten with my Mean Girls cast at. So it was just a really nice nostalgic trip and everyone’s so lovely in Toronto.”

Offscreen, Lohan is celebrating the holidays with husband Bader Shammas and their 3-year-old son, Luai. This year, traditions in her household are officially kicking off now that Luai has a better understanding of the holiday spirit.

“Traditions are starting officially, kind of, now with our son because he’s now more aware of Santa and reindeer. A tradition that we have is we always watch Rudolph together — the original old one, the old cartoon one,” Lohan told Us, adding that there’s “nothing better” than seeing her little one experience the holiday magic.

“We read a lot of Christmas books. Wrapping the presents is going to be the fun part,” she continued. “And just seeing his face on Christmas morning.”

Before the holidays are officially underway, Lohan partnered with Marshalls and well-known influential personalities and creators to create gift guides for all the different types of people (think: wellness, reality TV, travel and more) in shoppers’ lives.

“I love giving gifts and I think any time that we can make gifting easier in one space in one store is a blessing,” Lindsay told Us. “I love a thoughtful holiday campaign where we can help people get gifts for the ones that they love and the right kind of gifts instead of kind of wondering, ‘Oh my God, what do I get?’”

Fans of the Hunger Games franchise (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) were hyped to see a different side to Panem, especially those who read the Sunrise on the Reaping novel. One memorable moment is when Drusilla and Maysilee got into a slapping match on the train, and during a conversation from ET's Instagram, the two actresses joked about who had the better slap. Rockstar's GTA 6 features a massive open world to explore, and people continue to make new discoveries, including a terrifying killer clown Easter egg.

#3480. Are the Royals More Relatable Now Than Ever?

Prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power. Through their action-packed itinerary, which took them from Mumbai to New Delhi, the Prince and Princess of Wales have paved the way for a new style of royal tour.

From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.

According to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret. “None of us knew she was presenting an award on the night, or that she was going to speak. The auditorium was packed. There were about 5,000 people there. It’s been the biggest Earthshot yet, and you could see Catherine was nervous, but she delivered an absolutely brilliant speech. I’d say her best yet.

“It’s been wonderful for her to be here, supporting William, and you can see they’ve really had fun. Because of ongoing terror threats, there have been less walkabouts, but it’s been a very successful and varied tour, and I think, being shorter than most tours, it sets a new blueprint when it comes to royal tours for the couple in the future.”

Prince William and Princess Kate arrive to attend the Earthshot Prize awards night at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

There are seemingly already plans for another royal tour, says Myers.

“William let slip that Australia is on the cards next, and if that’s the case, I imagine they will go as a family. They don’t want to be away from their children for too long, and what a way it would be to win support for the monarchy Down Under,” Myers says.

According to royals insiders, there had been some nervousness around the trip after the couple’s disastrous tour of the Caribbean in March 2022, when their visit was overshadowed by calls for the UK to apologize for slavery. Then some of their photo calls, including one that involved the couple riding in an open-top Land Rover, led to accusations of the royals appearing colonial and out of touch.

“I think there has been a slight nervousness about how this tour would be received, but the reception has been really good,” Myers says. “The fact that William and Catherine have included a visit to New Delhi to see Prime Minister Modi is a clever move. While this is a private trip to promote Earthshot, the Foreign Office was keen for William to meet with the Indian prime minister, so they have packed that into the itinerary too.”

The visit to India has come at a time when the royals are on something of a charm offensive following a difficult year for the royal family, from Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest to what one palace insider calls “the ongoing soap opera” with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has not been charged and has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.)

William and Kate are keen to carve out their own initiatives and projects focusing on their major priorities, including the environment, children’s early years, and mental health. With the challenge of having Harry and Meghan carrying out their own engagements, the Prince and Princess of Wales have been careful to establish clear parameters that set them apart as working royals. In one telling moment while on an engagement in Mumbai, Kate was asked for an autograph. She politely declined, so as not to breach protocol, a clear contrast to the Duchess of Sussex, who has signed autographs in the past.

“Catherine was asked to sign an autograph, but she was right not to. It wasn’t a snub; it was just adhering to protocol. An autograph could be sold for money,” notes Dickie Arbiter, former press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II.

According to author Tom Bower, the royals are more relatable now than they were during the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, who famously never gave a press interview. In recent weeks, Prince William has appeared as a guest on The Graham Norton Show (to promote Earthshot), and he’s revealed how he drinks his cider and his love of wild swimming as part of his guest-editing stint for a recent issue of Country Life magazine.

“The royals are more relatable, perhaps, than they ever have been, but they are not celebrities. There’s a danger of being too relatable, too much ‘one of the people,’ which means they can lose some of their mystery,” Bower says.

“William will have been advised to do TV appearances and take on media opportunities to bolster his public image. Of course, it’s charming to hear these nuggets and see this side of the prince, but I do think there’s a need to see and hear more from William about his broader plans. Over the years, Charles has made huge efforts to appeal to all cultural aspects of society. I’m not sure William has done that. He’s got to find a way of connecting with everyone, not just the younger generation,” Bower adds.

The Earthshot Prize awards have been a powerful way of demonstrating that William doesn’t just talk the talk; he is insisting on action.

“The Earthshot is a master class in what needs to be done,” concludes Arbiter. “He’s pushing for environmental issues and climate change, and he’s getting people to do something about it. The fact that he is so well supported, and by so many high-profile people, shows his pulling power and influence.”

#3479. 9 People Injured During Mass Shooting at Concert Believed to Be Gang Related

Nine people were shot during a mass shooting at a private concert in California, and one person has been left in critical condition following the horrific incident.

The Tulare County Sheriff’s Office announced in a press release that the shooting broke out around 7:40 p.m. on Saturday, November 21, at a concert in Strathmore, California.

Officials said that an unspecified number of suspects started shooting at the crowd. No arrests have been announced as of time of publication.

One of the victims who was shot was a 26-year-old man, who was reportedly struck in the chest. He sustained severe injuries, which required him to undergo surgery. Officials said that the victim is currently in critical condition.

The sheriff’s office added that two other victims – who are 19 and 22 years old – also underwent surgery, while six people sustained minor injuries in the shooting.

“Initial reports indicated that the suspects opened fire into the crowd, hitting at least nine people. When Deputies arrived, they immediately began rendering first aid to the victims, while several others drove themselves to local hospitals for treatment,” the sheriff’s office wrote in a follow-up press release.

Authorities said that the shooting “may be gang-related,” but they did not elaborate on the theory or share if they have any suspects on their radar.

The Porterville Recorder reported that the shooting took place at a concert that was privately organized by the “norteño gang.” The outlet also reported that “it was also reported investigators had not determined if there was security at the event.”

The Tulare County Sheriff’s Office did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment when contacted about updates in the case.

The concert was attended by about 150 people, who gathered to watch rappers and other performers from neighboring states take the stage. San Jose-based rap artist Lazy Boy served as the event’s headliner.

An investigation into the incident remains ongoing as authorities work to determine how many shooters there were, who they are and if they had a motive.

The Tulare County Sheriff’s Office has asked that anyone with information regarding the incident contact the office at 559-733-6218.

The recent incident marks the 420th mass shootings in the United States so far in 2026, according to the Gun Violence Archive. The archive defines mass shootings as cases in which four or more victims are either wounded or killed after being shot at.

The series is pushing it with the extra 30 minutes.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I have watched enough seasons of Survivor to understand the game and have opinions, but not enough to drop Survivor lore. Therefore, I care about the show. It just doesn’t have some of the same dedication and loyalty from me as other reality TV shows. This may be why 2-hour episodes seem like another one of Survivor’s problems.

The last thing Survivor needs is 2-hour episodes.

From years of watching Big Brother, which you can also do with my Paramount+ subscription, I have seen what happens when a reality TV show has far more time than it needs: it misuses it. I don’t want to endure that with Survivor. It doesn’t need an extra 30 minutes. Nothing good can come out of that. We will likely get more fluff and filler, and things that don’t move the story along. More time doesn’t mean a show will effectively use it. We won’t get a season’s maximum potential with more time.

Additionally, Big Brother and similar shows aren’t the only ones to waste the extra time. Netflix reality TV shows play fast and loose with the runtimes. Sometimes the Netflix reality TV shows benefit from a few extra minutes. Other times it feels excessive and boring. I haven't been convinced any reality TV show needs two-hour episodes.

Survivor has worked out earlier issues with the 90-minute format; it doesn’t need to figure out 2 hours.

In the last few seasons, Survivor made some infuriating, questionable choices, so I don’t trust the show to make the best decisions with 2-hour episodes.

When Paramount+ announced a plan to lean more into reality TV, I expected more reality TV. They have announced a few new shows, but not nearly as many or as promising as expected. They have five TV shows under the Paramount+ banner that they could capitalize on with spin-offs. I will always scream to bring Big Brother: Over the Top and Big Brother: Reindeer Games back, but I am open to other ideas to expand that franchise, along with Survivor, The Amazing Race, The Challenge, and RuPaul’s Drag Race.

Instead of giving Survivor 2 hours, pair it with a new Survivor spin-off show to retain some of those viewers. Additionally, I actually prefer watching Survivor with The Amazing Race or another staple CBS reality TV show. I don’t just want a night of only Survivor. Now could be the perfect time to test out a shorter season of Big Brother with Survivor. Create a mini-Big Brother: All Stars spin-off series that only lasts for 30 days, similar to Survivor's length. This could bring in more viewers for each show.

I will gladly watch a three-hour movie (not gladly, but I will do it), but a TV show is pushing it with 2-hour episodes. If Survivor starts doing that, what’s to stop Big Brother, The Amazing Race, and some other reality TV shows?

I personally would be living a nightmare. We have to start limiting how many contestant packages we must see per episode. Change can be good, but this feels like another unnecessary update to the game and viewing.

#3476. GTA 6 Has A Super Mario Bros. Easter Egg, And It’s A Trip

Grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of fun Easter eggs--many of which tie back to earlier games in the series--but you can also find a few nods to other megapopular game franchises hiding within the vast map of Leonida. If you take a detour along the north side of Lummox County, you'll come across an area in the woods that looks like it'd be right at home in a Super Mario Bros. game, and you can even collect two distinct caps for your troubles--which might suggest that the greater Mario multiverse theory is true after all.

How to find the GTA 6 Super Mario Bros. Easter egg in GTA 6

You can mark this location on your map, as you can find the reference to the Nintendo mascot in Lummox County. It's up north from Mount Kalaga, at the end of a twisty road that seemingly goes nowhere:

Hit the bong, dude

Once you've arrived, scout the area for a purple tarp that has a bong sitting on it. Smoke it, get high, and climb the structure in front of you. You'll notice that there's a plume of smoke coming out of the one column, and if you stand in it, an invisible block will appear above your head.

Smash the block

Jump up, and you'll smash the block. You won't get any gold coins for your trouble, but you will get a nostalgic tune and two caps that reference Nintendo's favorite plumbers, Mario and Luigi.

Collect the caps

Each cap has an initial embroidered on it: "J" for Jason, "L" for Lucia. You can add them to your collection, or leave them to gather dust; it's up to you. 

As mentioned above, GTA 6 has references to a lot of pop culture. Someone at Rockstar Games is clearly a huge Dexter fan, Bigfoot is on the prowl, and I really wish I'd chosen the elevator without a killer clown inside it. For everything else on the biggest game of the year--and maybe even the decade--check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub.

#3475. 'Law & Order' Alum E.J. Carroll's Cause of Death Revealed After Collapse

Law & Order alum E.J. Carroll’s cause of death has been revealed after he collapsed in the streets of New York City on his way to a voiceover job.

Carroll died of a pulmonary embolism, his manager, Jon Mason, confirmed to Us. He was 66.

Us understands that Carroll recently underwent major surgery to correct a hernia issue. He had taken great lengths to improve his health before his death, including weight loss throughout his career.

Carroll was recovering from his surgery while on his way to a voiceover gig to add dialogue to a commercial he recently filmed with New York Knicks player Jalen Brunson and actress Quinta Brunson. He collapsed on the street en route to the job on Thursday, November 19.

A memorial service will be held in NYC on December 5.

Mason confirmed Carroll’s death in a statement shared on Saturday, November 21.

“When E.J. Carroll performed, it was impossible to take your eyes off him,” he said. “But his lasting legacy will be the kindness and generosity he showed his friends, fellow performers and even strangers.”

Mason added that Carroll was “as good a human being as it gets.”

Carroll’s close friend Jayce Bartok remembered the actor in a statement to Us after working together on the upcoming film A Delicate Arrangement.

“E.J. was my closest friend for the past 20 years. I met him on the set of a film I wrote, The Cake Eaters starring Kristen Stewart and Bruce Dern. I was preparing for a very dramatic scene, and E.J. and I shared a van. He was so sweet and genuine, he became connected to my family and professional life,” Bartok, 51, recalled.

The filmmaker continued, “We ended up working on numerous films together. He was an essential part of getting my film A Delicate Arrangement made, which is about a love affair between Vivien Leigh (played by Carla Gugino) and a local florist (Matthew Modine). He worked with Carla Gugino and David Hyde Pierce on the film, who both adored him, as anyone who seemed to work with him did.”

Bartok concluded, “His belief in the material allowed us to raise our post-production funding, and he refused to take any credit for this. He was a man of deep faith and charity, and spent every Thanksgiving serving the homeless. Ultimately, his passing on the way to an acting job personifies his commitment to his craft. It was his happiest place working, working with other actors, and supporting stories he wanted to tell.”

In her own statement, Gugino, 55, shared, “I had the great fortune of working with E.J. last winter in Philadelphia. He was a source of talent and light. My deepest condolences to his family and loved ones. RIP E.J. 🤍 🕊️.”

Carroll was known for his roles in Law & Order, Boardwalk Empire and The Deuce.
